title.zh: 卷四十九 列傳第三十九 庾杲之 王諶 孔珪 劉懷珍
title.en: Volume 49 Biographies 39: Yu Gaozhi, Wang Chen, Kong Gui, Liu Huaizhen
title.raw: 卷四十九 列傳第三十九 庾杲之 王諶 孔珪 劉懷珍 Volume 49 Biographies 39: Yu Gaozhi, Wang Chen, Kong Gui, Liu Huaizhen

sentences.zh: 庾杲之 王諶 孔珪 劉懷珍

translations.literal: Yu Gaozhi, Wang Chen, Kong Gui, Liu Huaizhen
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gaozhi, Wang Chen, Kong Gui, and Liu Huaizhen

sentences.zh: 杲之幼有孝行，宋司空劉勉見而奇之，謂曰：「見卿足使江漢崇望，杞梓發聲。

translations.literal: Gaozhi in youth had filial conduct; the Song Grand Minister Liu Mian saw him and marveled at him, saying, "Seeing you is enough to make the Jiang and Han hold you in high esteem and the catalpa and plane trees give forth their sound."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozhi showed filial devotion from childhood. When Liu Mian, Grand Minister of the Song, met him he was struck with wonder and said, "At the sight of you the Yangtze and Han regions would lift their eyes in respect, and the finest timber would find its voice."

sentences.zh: 」解褐奉朝請，稍遷尚書駕部郎。

translations.literal: " He left plain dress to become a Palace Attendant and was gradually promoted to Director of the Imperial Carriage Department in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: " He left commoner status to become a Palace Attendant and was gradually promoted to Director of the Imperial Carriage Department in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 清貧自業，食唯有韭葅瀹韭生韭雜菜。

translations.literal: Poor and pure in his occupation, his food consisted only of pickled leeks, boiled leeks, raw leeks, and mixed vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in deliberate poverty; his entire diet was leeks in every form—pickled, boiled, and raw—together with other simple vegetables.

sentences.zh: 任昉嘗戲之曰：「誰謂庾郎貧，食鮭嘗有二十七種。」

translations.literal: Ren Fang once joked with him, saying, "Who says Master Yu is poor? When he eats salmon he has twenty-seven kinds."
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fang once teased him: "Who says Lord Yu is poor? His 'salmon' comes in twenty-seven varieties."

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 王儉謂人曰：「昔袁公作衛軍，欲用我為長史，雖不獲就，要是意向如此。

translations.literal: Wang Jian said to others, "In the past when Duke Yuan served as Defender-General, he wished to employ me as chief clerk; though I did not obtain the post, that was nonetheless his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian told others, "When Duke Yuan was Defender-General he wanted me as his chief clerk. I never took the post, but that was clearly what he had in mind.

sentences.zh: 今亦應須如我輩人也。

translations.literal: Now too one ought to need people of our sort."
translations.idiomatic: Today as well one needs men of our stamp."

sentences.zh: 」乃用杲之為衛將軍長史。

translations.literal: " He then appointed Gaozhi chief clerk to the Defender-General.
translations.idiomatic: " On that basis he appointed Gaozhi chief clerk to the Defender-General.

sentences.zh: 安陸侯蕭緬與儉書曰：「盛府元僚，實難其選。

translations.literal: Marquis of Anlu Xiao Mian wrote to Jian, saying, "For the chief aide of a great establishment, the choice is truly hard.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Anlu, Xiao Mian, wrote to Jian: "Choosing the chief aide for so great a household is no easy matter.

sentences.zh: 庾景行泛淥水，依芙蓉，何其麗也。

translations.literal: Yu Jingxing floats on the clear water, leaning on the lotus—how beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jingxing drifts on the clear stream, resting against the lotus—how splendid!

sentences.zh: 」時人以入儉府為蓮花池，故緬書美之。

translations.literal: " People of the time called entering Jian's establishment the Lotus Pond, and so Mian's letter praised him.
translations.idiomatic: " Entering Jian's household was known as the Lotus Pond, which is why Mian's letter lavished such praise on him.

sentences.zh: 歷位黃門吏部郎，御史中丞，參大選。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Yellow Gate Attendant, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Censor-in-Chief, and took part in the great selections.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Yellow Gate Attendant, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Censor-in-Chief, and participated in the senior appointments.

sentences.zh: 美容質，善言笑。

translations.literal: He had a handsome appearance and was skilled in speech and laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome in bearing, he was gifted at conversation and wit.

sentences.zh: 嘗兼侍中夾侍，柳世隆在御坐，謂齊武帝曰：「庾杲之為蟬冕所映，彌有華采，陛下故當與其即真。

translations.literal: Once, while serving concurrently as Attendant-in-Ordinary flanking the throne, Liu Shilong was at the imperial seat and said to Emperor Wu of Qi, "Yu Gaozhi, reflected in the cicada crown and court robes, has all the more splendor; Your Majesty ought therefore to grant him full appointment."
translations.idiomatic: Once, while doubling as Attendant-in-Ordinary beside the throne, Liu Shilong, seated with the emperor, told Emperor Wu of Qi, "Yu Gaozhi glows in his court regalia—Your Majesty should give him the full post without delay."

sentences.zh: 」上甚悅。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 王儉仍曰：「國家以杲之清美，所以許其假職。

translations.literal: Wang Jian then said, "The state, because Gaozhi is pure and fine, therefore allowed him a provisional post.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian added, "The court granted Gaozhi only a provisional appointment because of his pure and refined character.

sentences.zh: 若以其即真，當在胡諧之後。

translations.literal: If he were to receive full appointment, it should be after Hu Xie."
translations.idiomatic: If he were confirmed in office, he would still rank behind Hu Xie."

sentences.zh: 」武帝嘗與朝臣商略，酒後謂群臣曰：「我後當得何諡？

translations.literal: " Emperor Wu once discussed matters with the court ministers, and after wine said to the assembled officials, "What posthumous title shall I receive hereafter?"
translations.idiomatic: " Once, after drinking with his ministers, Emperor Wu asked the court, "What posthumous title will I earn when I am gone?"

sentences.zh: 」群臣莫有答者。

translations.literal: " None of the ministers had an answer.
translations.idiomatic: " No one in the assembly replied.

sentences.zh: 王儉因目杲之，從容曰：「陛下壽等南山，方與日月齊明，千載之後，豈是臣子輕所仰量。

translations.literal: Wang Jian thereupon looked at Gaozhi, who said at ease, "Your Majesty's life equals the southern mountain; you are just now level in brightness with sun and moon—a thousand years hence, how could subjects lightly presume to measure it?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian glanced at Gaozhi, who answered calmly, "Your Majesty's span equals Mount Zhongnan; your glory matches the sun and moon. A thousand years from now, what subject would dare guess at such things?"

sentences.zh: 」時人雅歎其辯答。

translations.literal: " People of the time admired his eloquent reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Contemporaries praised his tactful answer.

sentences.zh: 杲之嘗兼主客郎對魏使，使問杲之曰：「百姓那得家家題門帖賣宅？

translations.literal: Gaozhi once concurrently served as Director of Guests in receiving the Wei envoy; the envoy asked Gaozhi, "How is it that every household posts notices on the door selling their homes?"
translations.idiomatic: While doubling as Director of Guests, Gaozhi received a Wei envoy who asked, "Why does every household in your land post a notice on the gate offering its house for sale?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「朝廷既欲掃蕩京洛，克復神州，所以家家賣宅耳。

translations.literal: " He answered, "The court already intends to sweep clean Luoyang and recover the Central Land, and so every household is selling its home."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Because the court means to sweep the north clean, retake Luoyang, and recover the heartland—every family is selling up to move north."

sentences.zh: 」魏使縮鼻而不答。

translations.literal: " The Wei envoy wrinkled his nose and made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy from Wei sniffed and fell silent.

sentences.zh: 時諸王年少，不得妄稱接人，敕杲之及濟陽江淹五日一詣諸王，使申遊好。

translations.literal: At that time the princes were young and might not recklessly claim to receive people; an edict ordered Gaozhi and Jiang Yan of Jiyang to visit the princes once every five days to extend friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: The princes were still young and forbidden to receive visitors at will; the court ordered Gaozhi and Jiang Yan of Jiyang to call on them every five days to keep friendly ties.

sentences.zh: 再遷尚書吏部郎，參大選事，太子右衛率，加通直常侍。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel in the Ministry of Works, took part in the great selections, became Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, and was given the additional title of Regular Attendant with Unimpeded Access.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, took part in senior appointments, became Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, and received the additional title of Regular Attendant with Unimpeded Access.

sentences.zh: 九年卒，上甚惜之，諡曰貞子。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died; the emperor deeply regretted it and gave him the posthumous title Chaste Master.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year; the emperor mourned him deeply and posthumously named him Master of Integrity.

sentences.zh: 蓽字休野，杲之叔父也。

translations.literal: Bi, style name Xiuye, was Gaozhi's uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Bi, whose style was Xiuye, was Gaozhi's uncle.

sentences.zh: 仕齊為驃騎功曹史。

translations.literal: He served Qi as a clerk in the Rapid Cavalry commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he served as clerk in the office of the Rapid Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 博涉群書，有口辯。

translations.literal: He broadly ranged through the classics and had eloquence in speech.
translations.idiomatic: Widely read and quick with his tongue, he was a formidable debater.

sentences.zh: 永明中與魏和親，以蓽兼散騎常侍，報使還，拜散騎侍郎、知東宮管記事。

translations.literal: During Yongming, when peace was made with Wei, Bi was appointed concurrent Regular Attendant of the Unmounted Retinue as returning envoy; on his return he was made Gentleman of the Unmounted Retinue and put in charge of the Eastern Palace record office.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming, when Qi made peace with Wei, Bi served concurrently as Regular Attendant of the Unmounted Retinue on the return embassy. Back home he was made Gentleman of the Unmounted Retinue and superintendent of the crown prince's record office.

sentences.zh: 後為荊州別駕，前後紀綱皆致富饒，蓽再為之，清身率下，杜絕請托，布被蔬食，妻子不免饑寒。

translations.literal: Later he became Vice Governor of Jing Province; those before and after who held the chief staff all grew wealthy, but when Bi held the post a second time he kept his person pure and led subordinates by example, cutting off all requests and favors; with cloth quilts and vegetable food, his wife and children could not escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Vice Governor of Jing Province. Every chief aide before and after him had grown rich; Bi, serving a second term, lived cleanly, led by example, refused all patronage, slept under cotton quilts and ate vegetables—and his wife and children still knew hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 齊明帝聞而嘉焉，手敕褒美，州裏榮之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Qi heard and commended it, personally drafting an edict of praise; the province honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Qi heard of it with approval and wrote a personal edict of praise; the whole province took pride in him.

sentences.zh: 初，梁州人益州刺史鄧元起功勳甚著，名地卑瑣，願名掛士流。

translations.literal: Earlier, Deng Yuanqi of Liang Province, Governor of Yi, had very distinguished merit; his name and standing were low and mean, yet he wished his name to hang among the gentry stream.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Deng Yuanqi of Liangzhou, Governor of Yi, had won great distinction in battle, but his birth was humble and he longed to have his name listed among the gentry.

sentences.zh: 時始興忠武王憺為州將，元起位已高，而解巾不先州官，則不為鄉里所悉，元起乞上籍出身州從事，憺命蓽用之，蓽不從。

translations.literal: At the time the Loyal King of Shixing, Xiao Dan, was provincial commander; Yuanqi's rank was already high, but unless he removed his headcloth before the provincial officials he would not be known in his native place; Yuanqi begged to register his origin as a provincial clerk, Dan ordered Bi to employ him, and Bi refused.
translations.idiomatic: The Loyal King of Shixing, Xiao Dan, was then provincial commander. Yuanqi's rank was already high, yet unless he entered the local register through a provincial post his neighbors would not acknowledge him. He asked to be enrolled as a provincial clerk; Dan ordered Bi to appoint him, and Bi refused.

sentences.zh: 憺大怒，召蓽責之曰：「元起已經我府，卿何為苟惜從事？

translations.literal: Dan was greatly angered, summoned Bi, and reproached him, saying, "Yuanqi has already passed through my establishment—why do you stingily withhold a clerkship from him?"
translations.idiomatic: Dan flew into a rage, summoned Bi, and rebuked him: "Yuanqi has already served in my household—why begrudge him a clerkship?"

sentences.zh: 」蓽曰：「府是尊府，州是蓽州，宜須品藻。

translations.literal: " Bi said, "Your establishment is the honored establishment; the province is Bi's province—one ought to judge and select."
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "Your household is yours to command; this province is mine to judge—I must weigh the man's fitness."

sentences.zh: 」憺不能折，遂止。

translations.literal: " Dan could not refute him and let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: " Dan could not overcome him and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 累遷會稽郡丞，行郡府事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Assistant Administrator of Kuaiji Commandery and acted in the affairs of the commandery seat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Assistant Administrator of Kuaiji and ran the commandery government.

sentences.zh: 時承雕弊之後，百姓凶荒，米斗至數千，人多流散。

translations.literal: The time followed on carved exhaustion; the people were in cruel famine, rice reached several thousand per dou, and many drifted away.
translations.idiomatic: He took office after years of ruin; famine gripped the land, grain sold for thousands per dou, and the people scattered in flight.

sentences.zh: 蓽撫循甚有理，唯守公祿，清節愈厲，至有經日不舉火。

translations.literal: Bi comforted and guided with great reason, kept only his official salary, and his pure integrity grew stricter—at times going whole days without lighting a fire.
translations.idiomatic: Bi governed with humane order, lived only on his official salary, and grew ever stricter in integrity—sometimes going a full day without kindling his stove.

sentences.zh: 太守永陽王聞而饋之，蓽謝不受。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yongyang, the commandery administrator, heard and sent him gifts; Bi declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yongyang, as commandery administrator, heard and sent provisions; Bi thanked him and refused.

sentences.zh: 天監元年卒，停屍無以斂，柩不能歸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian he died; the corpse lay with nothing to enshroud it, and the coffin could not be returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Tianjian; his family had nothing to lay him out in, and they could not even bring his coffin home.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝聞之，詔賜絹百疋，穀五百斛。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang heard and ordered a gift of one hundred bolts of silk and five hundred hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang heard and ordered a grant of one hundred bolts of silk and five hundred hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 子喬復仕為荊州別駕，時元帝為荊州刺史，而州人範興話以寒賤仕叨九流，選為州主簿，又皇太子令及之，故元帝勒喬聽興話到職。

translations.literal: His son Qiao again served as Vice Governor of Jing; at the time Emperor Yuan was Governor of Jing, and a man of the province, Fan Xinghua, through humble and base service had presumptuously entered the nine ranks and was selected as provincial chief clerk; the crown prince also ordered it, and so Emperor Yuan urged Qiao to let Xinghua take office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiao also served as Vice Governor of Jing when Emperor Yuan was governor. Fan Xinghua, a local man of humble birth, had wrangled his way into the nine ranks and been made provincial chief clerk at the crown prince's order; Emperor Yuan pressed Qiao to let Xinghua take up the post.

sentences.zh: 及屬元日，府州朝賀，喬不肯就列，曰：「庾喬忝為端右，不能與小人範興話為雁行。

translations.literal: When New Year's Day came, the prefectural and provincial offices paid court congratulations; Qiao refused to take his place in the ranks, saying, "Yu Qiao, though unworthily at the head of the right, cannot stand in goose formation with the petty man Fan Xinghua."
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day, when the prefectural and provincial staffs assembled for congratulations, Qiao refused to take his place and said, "Though I unworthily hold the chief post on the right, I cannot stand in rank beside the lowborn Fan Xinghua."

sentences.zh: 」元帝聞，乃進喬而停興話。

translations.literal: " Emperor Yuan heard and thereupon advanced Qiao and halted Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Yuan heard, he promoted Qiao and blocked Xinghua's appointment.

sentences.zh: 興話羞慚還家憤卒。

translations.literal: Xinghua, ashamed, returned home and died in indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated, Xinghua went home and died of rage.

sentences.zh: 世以喬為不墜家風。

translations.literal: The age considered Qiao as not letting the family style fall.
translations.idiomatic: The world judged that Qiao had not betrayed his family's honor.

sentences.zh: 喬子敻少聰慧，家富於財，好賓客，食必列鼎。

translations.literal: Qiao's son Xuan from youth was clever and wise; the family was rich in wealth, loved guests, and at meals always set out tripods.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao's son Xuan was clever from boyhood; the family was wealthy, loved to entertain, and always set a full banquet with ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 又狀貌豐美，頤頰開張，人皆謂敻必為方伯，無餒乏之慮。

translations.literal: Moreover his form and appearance were full and beautiful, his cheeks and jaws broad and open; everyone said Xuan would surely become a regional lord and had no worry of hunger or want.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome and broad of face, everyone said he was destined for a regional governorship and would never know want.

sentences.zh: 及魏克江陵，卒致餓死。

translations.literal: When Wei captured Jiangling, he in the end came to die of starvation.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei took Jiangling, he ended up starving to death.

sentences.zh: 時又有水軍都督褚蘿面甚尖危，有從理入口，竟保衣食而終。

translations.literal: At the time there was also the naval commander Chu Luo, whose face was very sharp and precipitous, with a crease running into his mouth; he in the end preserved food and clothing to the end.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the naval commander Chu Luo, whose face was sharp and gaunt with a crease running into his mouth—yet he kept himself fed and clothed to the end.

sentences.zh: 王諶字仲和，東海郯人，晉少傅雅玄孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Chen, style name Zhonghe, was a man of Tan in Donghai, great-great-grandson of Wang Ya, Junior Tutor of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen, styled Zhonghe, came from Tan in Donghai and was the great-great-grandson of Jin's Junior Tutor Wang Ya.

sentences.zh: 祖慶，員外常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qing was an Extraordinary Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qing served as Extraordinary Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 父元閔，護軍司馬。

translations.literal: His father Yuanmin was a marshal of the Protector Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanmin was marshal on the staff of the Protector Army.

sentences.zh: 宋大明中，沈曇慶為徐州，辟諶為迎主簿，又為州迎從事，湘東王彧國常侍，鎮北行參軍。

translations.literal: In the Daming era of Song, when Shen Tanqing was in Xuzhou, he recruited Chen as welcoming chief clerk, then as provincial welcoming attendant, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Principality of Xiangdong under Prince Yu, and Acting Army Aide on the Northern Defense staff.
translations.idiomatic: During Song's Daming era, when Shen Tanqing governed Xuzhou, he recruited Chen as welcoming chief clerk, then as provincial welcoming attendant, as Attendant-in-Ordinary to Prince Yu of Xiangdong, and as acting army aide on the northern defense staff.

sentences.zh: 及彧即帝位，是為明帝，除司徒參軍，帶薛令，兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Yu ascended the throne as Emperor Ming, Chen was made an aide on the Minister of Education's staff, concurrently Magistrate of Xue, and concurrently Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu took the throne as Emperor Ming, Chen was appointed aide on the Minister of Education's staff, concurrent magistrate of Xue, and concurrent Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 諶有學義，見親遇，常在左右。

translations.literal: Chen had learning and principle, was treated with intimate favor, and was constantly at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: Learned and principled, Chen won the emperor's trust and was rarely away from his side.

sentences.zh: 帝所行慘僻，諶屢諫不從，請退，坐此系尚方。

translations.literal: The emperor's conduct was cruel and perverse; Chen repeatedly remonstrated but was not obeyed, requested withdrawal, and for this was imprisoned in the Imperial Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's rule grew cruel and arbitrary; Chen remonstrated again and again without success, asked to resign, and for that was sent to the Imperial Workshop prison.

sentences.zh: 後拜中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明帝好圍棋，置圍棋州邑，以建安王休仁為圍棋州都大中正，諶與太子右率沈勃、尚書水部郎庾珪之、彭城丞王抗四人為小中正，朝請褚思莊、傅楚之為清定訪問。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming loved weiqi and established weiqi prefectures and districts; he made Prince of Jian'an Xiuren Grand Rectifier of the Weiqi Prefecture, and Chen together with the crown prince's Right Commandant Shen Bo, Director of the Water Bureau in the Ministry of Works Gui Zhi, and Assistant Magistrate of Pengcheng Wang Kang were four lesser rectifiers; Palace Attendants Chu Sizhuang and Fu Chuzhi were clear-ranking investigators.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming was devoted to weiqi and created a weiqi 'prefecture' system. He named Prince Xiuren of Jian'an its grand rectifier; Chen, Shen Bo (Right Commandant to the crown prince), Gui Zhi (Director of the Water Bureau), and Wang Kang (assistant magistrate of Pengcheng) served as lesser rectifiers; Chu Sizhuang and Fu Chuzhi were appointed ranking investigators.

sentences.zh: 後為尚書左丞，領東觀祭酒，即明帝所置總明觀也。

translations.literal: Later he was Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and concurrently Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion—that is, the Zongming Observatory established by Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion—the Zongming Observatory that Emperor Ming had founded.

sentences.zh: 遷黃門郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 齊永明初，累遷豫章王太尉司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongming in Qi he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Marshal on the staff of the Prince of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qi's Yongming era he rose to Grand Marshal on the staff of the Prince of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 武帝與諶相遇于宋明之世，甚委任之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu and Chen had met in the era of Song's Emperor Ming and greatly entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu had known Chen since the reign of Song's Emperor Ming and placed great trust in him.

sentences.zh: 曆黃門郎，領驍騎將軍，太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He passed through Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry, and Regular Attendant to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry, and Regular Attendant to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 諶貞正和謹，朝廷稱為善人，多與之厚。

translations.literal: Chen was upright, correct, harmonious, and careful; the court called him a good man, and many were close with him.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, temperate, and careful, Chen was known at court as a good man, and many cultivated deep friendship with him.

sentences.zh: 八年，轉冠軍將軍、長沙王車騎長史，徙廬江王中軍長史，又徙西陽王子明征虜長史，行南兗府州事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to General of the Champions and chief clerk on the chariots-and-cavalry staff of the Prince of Changsha, moved to chief clerk on the central army staff of the Prince of Lujiang, then moved again to chief clerk on the campaign-against-the-barbarians staff of Ziming, Prince of Xiyang, acting in the affairs of the southern Yan prefecture and province.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became General of the Champions and chief clerk to the Prince of Changsha's chariot-and-cavalry command, then chief clerk on the Prince of Lujiang's central army staff, then chief clerk to Ziming, Prince of Xiyang, on his campaign staff, acting for the southern Yan prefecture and province.

sentences.zh: 諶少貧，常自紡績，及通貴後，每為人說之，世稱其達。

translations.literal: Chen in youth was poor and often spun thread himself; after reaching high rank he would tell people of it, and the age praised his openness.
translations.idiomatic: Chen had been poor in youth and often spun hemp himself; after he rose high he still told the story openly, and the world called him magnanimous.

sentences.zh: 九年卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year.

sentences.zh: 諶從叔摛，以博學見知。

translations.literal: Chen's paternal uncle's son Chi was known for broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's cousin Chi was famed for erudition.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王儉嘗集才學之士，總校虛實，類物隸之，謂之隸事，自此始也。

translations.literal: Wang Jian, Minister of Works, once gathered men of talent and learning to collate what was empty and what was real, classify things and attach them in clerical form—called "clerical matters"—and from this it began.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, Minister of Works, once gathered scholars to test fact against fancy, matching things to parallel citations in an exercise called "clerical matters"—and with that the fashion began.

sentences.zh: 儉嘗使賓客隸事多者賞之，事皆窮，唯廬江何憲為勝，乃賞以五花簟、白團扇。

translations.literal: Jian once had his guests compete in clerical matters, rewarding whoever had the most; all were exhausted, and only He Xian of Lujiang was victorious, whereupon he rewarded him with a five-flower mat and a white round fan.
translations.idiomatic: Jian once set his guests to compete at clerical matters, promising a prize to whoever produced the most parallels; everyone was stumped except He Xian of Lujiang, who won a five-color mat and a white round fan.

sentences.zh: 坐簟執扇，容氣甚自得。

translations.literal: Seated on the mat and holding the fan, his bearing and air were very self-satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: He sat on the mat with the fan in hand, looking thoroughly pleased with himself.

sentences.zh: 摛後至，儉以所隸示之，曰：「卿能奪之乎？

translations.literal: Chi arrived later; Jian showed him the clerical pieces and said, "Can you seize them from him?"
translations.idiomatic: Chi arrived late; Jian showed him the winning parallels and asked, "Can you take the prize from him?"

sentences.zh: 」摛操筆便成，文章既奧，辭亦華美，舉坐擊賞。

translations.literal: " Chi took up the brush and at once completed it; the writing was both profound and the diction splendid; the whole assembly struck their hands in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: " Chi took brush in hand and finished on the spot—profound in substance, splendid in style—and the whole room applauded.

sentences.zh: 摛乃命左右抽憲簟，手自掣取扇，登車而去。

translations.literal: Chi then ordered his attendants to pull away Xian's mat, personally snatched the fan, mounted his carriage, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Chi ordered his servants to pull the mat from under Xian, seized the fan himself, climbed into his carriage, and drove away.

sentences.zh: 儉笑曰：「所謂大力者負之而趨。

translations.literal: Jian laughed and said, "What is called 'the strong man carries it and hurries off.'"
translations.idiomatic: Jian laughed and quoted the old line: "The strong man hoists it on his back and runs."

sentences.zh: 」竟陵王子良校試諸學士，唯摛問無不對。

translations.literal: " Prince Ziliang of Jingling examined and tested the various scholars; only Chi, to whatever he was asked, had no failure to answer.
translations.idiomatic: " When Prince Ziliang of Jingling tested his scholars, Chi alone answered every question.

sentences.zh: 為秣陵令，清直，請謁不行。

translations.literal: He was Magistrate of Moling, pure and upright; requests and visits were not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Moling he was incorruptible and refused all private petitions.

sentences.zh: 羽林隊主潘敞有寵二宮，勢傾人主。

translations.literal: Pan Chang, captain of the Feathered Forest guard, had favor with both palaces and power that tilted toward the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Chang, captain of the Feathered Forest guard, enjoyed favor in both palaces and wielded power that rivaled the throne.

sentences.zh: 婦弟犯法，敞為之請摛，摛投書於地，更鞭四十。

translations.literal: His wife's younger brother violated the law; Chang pleaded for him with Chi; Chi threw the letter on the ground and had him flogged forty more strokes.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife's brother broke the law, Chang interceded with Chi, who threw the petition on the ground and added forty lashes.

sentences.zh: 敞怒譖之，明日而見代。

translations.literal: Chang in anger slandered him, and the next day Chi was replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Chang slandered him in a rage, and Chi was removed the next day.

sentences.zh: 永明八年，天忽黃色照地，眾莫能解。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongming the sky suddenly turned yellow and shone on the ground; none could explain it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yongming the sky turned yellow and bathed the earth; no one could explain it.

sentences.zh: 司徒法曹王融上金天頌。

translations.literal: Wang Rong of the Minister of Education's legal bureau submitted a hymn to the Golden Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong of the Minister of Education's legal bureau submitted a hymn to the Golden Heaven.

sentences.zh: 摛曰：「是非金天，所謂榮光。

translations.literal: Chi said, "This is not the Golden Heaven; it is what is called 'glorious light.'"
translations.idiomatic: Chi said, "That is not the Golden Heaven—it is what is called glorious light."

sentences.zh: 」武帝大悅，用為永陽郡。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wu was greatly pleased and employed him as Administrator of Yongyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Wu was delighted and appointed him administrator of Yongyang.

sentences.zh: 後卒于尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Later he died while Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He later died in office as Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 何憲字子思，廬江灊人。

translations.literal: He Xian, style name Zisi, was a man of Qian in Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He Xian, styled Zisi, came from Qian in Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 博涉該通，群籍畢覽，天閣寶秘，人間散逸，無遺漏焉。

translations.literal: Broadly ranging and comprehensively penetrating, he completely perused the classics; celestial vault treasures and secrets, and works scattered and lost among men—none escaped him.
translations.idiomatic: Immensely learned, he had read every classic in the imperial archives and every stray text still circulating among men—nothing had escaped him.

sentences.zh: 任昉、劉渢共執秘閣四部書，試問其所知，自甲至丁，書說一事，並敘述作之體，連日累夜，莫見所遺。

translations.literal: Ren Fang and Liu Jun together held the four divisions of books in the Secret Pavilion and tested what he knew; from jia to ding, for each book they cited one matter and also narrated the form of composition—day after day, night after night, none saw what he had missed.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fang and Liu Jun took the four divisions of the Secret Pavilion and quizzed him book by book—from jia through ding—on a fact from each work and on its literary form. For days and nights they found nothing he did not know.

sentences.zh: 宗人何遁，退讓士也，見而美之，願與為友。

translations.literal: His clansman He Dun was a yielding and retiring gentleman; seeing him he admired him and wished to become his friend.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman He Dun, a modest and retiring gentleman, admired him on sight and asked to be his friend.

sentences.zh: 憲位本州別駕，國子博士。

translations.literal: Xian's posts were Vice Governor of his native province and Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Xian held the posts of Vice Governor of his home province and Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 永明十年使于魏。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongming he was envoy to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yongming he served as envoy to Wei.

sentences.zh: 時又有孔逖字世遠，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: At the time there was also Kong Ti, style name Shiyuan, a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Kong Ti, styled Shiyuan, from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 好典故學，與王儉至交。

translations.literal: He loved the study of classical precedents and was a close friend of Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He loved antiquarian learning and was Wang Jian's closest friend.

sentences.zh: 升明中為齊台尚書儀曹郎，屢箴闕禮，多見信納。

translations.literal: During Shengming he was Director of Rites in the Qi Secretariat; he repeatedly admonished on lapses in ritual, and much was trusted and adopted.
translations.idiomatic: During Shengming he was Director of Rites on the Qi Secretariat staff; he repeatedly corrected lapses in ceremonial law, and the court often took his advice.

sentences.zh: 上謂王儉曰：「逖真所謂儀曹，不忝厥職也。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Wang Jian, "Ti is truly what is called a Director of Rites—he does not disgrace his office."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Wang Jian, "Ti is a true Director of Rites—he does honor to the post."

sentences.zh: 」儉為宰相，逖常謀議幄帳，每及選用，頗失鄉曲情。

translations.literal: " Jian was chancellor; Ti often joined deliberation in the command tent, and whenever selection and appointment were discussed, he often lost the regard of his native-place fellows.
translations.idiomatic: "Once Wang Jian became chief minister, Kong Ti was constantly at his side in council; but whenever offices were filled, he often offended the expectations of his home district.

sentences.zh: 儉從容啟上曰：「臣有孔逖，猶陛下之有臣。

translations.literal: Jian calmly reported to the sovereign, saying: "Your subject has Kong Ti, just as Your Majesty has your subject.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian spoke to the throne with easy composure: "I have Kong Ti, as Your Majesty has me.

sentences.zh: 」永明中為太子家令卒。

translations.literal: " In the Yongming era he died while serving as Director of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: "He passed away in the Yongming period while holding the post of Director of the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時人呼孔逖何憲為王儉三公。

translations.literal: Men of the time called Kong Ti and He Xian the Three Dukes of Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries nicknamed Kong Ti and He Xian Wang Jian's Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 及卒，儉惜之，為撰祭文。

translations.literal: When he died, Jian regretted him and composed a sacrificial text for him.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Wang Jian mourned the loss and wrote a funeral elegy in his honor.

sentences.zh: 孔珪字德璋，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Kong Gui, style name Dezheng, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Gui, styled Dezheng, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 祖道隆，位侍中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dao Long reached the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kong Dao Long had served as Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 父靈產，泰始中，晉安太守，有隱遁之志。

translations.literal: His father Lingchan, in the Taishi era, was Governor of Jin'an and harbored a wish to withdraw and live in seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lingchan, who in the Taishi period had been governor of Jin'an, longed to withdraw from the world.

sentences.zh: 于禹井山立館，事道精篤。

translations.literal: He established a lodge on Yujing Mountain and served the Way with deep devotion.
translations.idiomatic: On Yujing Mountain he built a retreat and practiced the Way with fervent single-mindedness.

sentences.zh: 吉日于靜屋四向朝拜，涕泣滂沱。

translations.literal: On auspicious days, in a quiet chamber he worshipped toward the four directions, and his tears poured down in torrents.
translations.idiomatic: On ritual days he would worship toward all four quarters from a silent room, weeping until his face streamed with tears.

sentences.zh: 東出過錢唐北郭，輒於舟中遙拜杜子恭墓。

translations.literal: When traveling east and passing the north suburb of Qiantang, he would bow from his boat toward the tomb of Du Zigong.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went east and passed the northern outskirts of Qiantang, he would bow from the boat toward Du Zigong's grave.

sentences.zh: 自此至都，東向坐，不敢背側。

translations.literal: From that point until he reached the capital, he sat facing east and dared not turn his back or sit sideways.
translations.idiomatic: From then until he arrived at court he always sat facing east, never turning his back or sitting askew.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，為中散大夫，頗解星文，好術數。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhui era he was a Palace Attendant, understood the stars well, and loved numerology and prognostication.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanhui he served as Palace Attendant; he was well versed in astronomy and delighted in occult calculation.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝輔政，沈攸之起兵，靈產白高帝曰：「攸之兵眾雖強，以天時冥數而觀，無能為也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi served as regent and Shen Youzhi raised troops, Lingchan told the emperor, "Though Youzhi's host is strong in numbers, viewed through heaven's seasons and the hidden reckoning of fate, he can accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: While the future Emperor Gao of Qi was regent and Shen Youzhi rebelled, Lingchan told him, "For all Youzhi's strength in arms, the signs of heaven and the dark arithmetic of fate show he will come to nothing.

sentences.zh: 」高帝驗其言，擢遷光祿大夫，以簏盛靈產上靈台，令其占候。

translations.literal: " The emperor verified his words, promoted him to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, had Lingchan carried up the Spirit Terrace in a bamboo hamper, and ordered him to observe and prognosticate.
translations.idiomatic: "When events proved him right, the emperor raised him to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, had him borne up the Spirit Terrace in a litter, and charged him with reading the heavens.

sentences.zh: 餉靈產白羽扇、素隱几，曰：「君有古人之風，故贈君古人之服。

translations.literal: He presented Lingchan with a white feather fan and a plain reclining stool, saying, "You have the air of the ancients; therefore I give you the garb of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Lingchan a white feather fan and a plain armrest, saying, "You carry yourself like a man of old—so I offer you the trappings of old.

sentences.zh: 」當世榮之。

translations.literal: " The age honored this.
translations.idiomatic: "The court took this as a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 珪少學涉有美譽，太守王僧虔見而重之，引為主簿。

translations.literal: Gui in youth was broadly learned and enjoyed a fine reputation; the Governor Wang Sengqian saw him, valued him, and appointed him Registrar.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Kong Gui was widely read and highly regarded; Governor Wang Sengqian took notice of him and made him his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，再遷殿中郎。

translations.literal: He was recommended as a xiucai and was twice promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as a xiucai, he rose twice to the post of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 高帝為驃騎，取為記室參軍，與江淹對掌辭筆。

translations.literal: When the emperor was Cavalry General, he took him as Record Keeper in his staff and paired him with Jiang Yan to share charge of the writing brush.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Gao was General of Agile Cavalry, he made Kong Gui his secretarial aide and paired him with Jiang Yan to handle official prose.

sentences.zh: 為尚書左丞，父憂去官。

translations.literal: He served as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and left office on his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He became Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, then resigned to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 與兄仲智還居父山舍。

translations.literal: With his elder brother Zhongzhi he returned to dwell in their father's mountain lodge.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Zhongzhi went back to live in their father's mountain retreat.

sentences.zh: 仲智妾李氏驕妒無禮，珪白太守王敬則殺之。

translations.literal: Zhongzhi's concubine, Lady Li, was arrogant, jealous, and without propriety; Gui reported to the Governor Wang Jingze, who had her put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi's concubine Lady Li was insolent, jealous, and ill-mannered; Kong Gui denounced her to Governor Wang Jingze, who ordered her executed.

sentences.zh: 永明中，歷位黃門郎，太子中庶子，廷尉。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era he successively held the posts of Yellow Gate Attendant, Middle Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming he served in turn as Yellow Gate Attendant, Middle Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 江左承用晉時張、杜律二十卷，武帝留心法令，數訊囚徒，詔獄官詳正舊注。

translations.literal: South of the Yangtze continued to use the twenty-scroll Zhang-Du code of Jin times; Emperor Wu attended closely to penal law, often interrogated prisoners, and ordered prison officials to collate and correct the old commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: The court south of the Yangtze still followed the twenty-fascicle penal code of Zhang and Du from Jin; Emperor Wu took a keen interest in statutes, repeatedly tried prisoners himself, and ordered judicial officers to revise the old glosses.

sentences.zh: 先是尚書刪定郎王植撰定律，奏之，削其煩害，錄其允衷，取張斐注七百三十一條，杜預注七百九十一條，或二家兩釋於義乃備者，又取一百七條，其注相同者取一百三條，集為一書，凡一千七百三十二條，為二十卷。

translations.literal: Earlier the Editing and Fixing Clerk of the Secretariat, Wang Zhi, had composed and fixed the statutes and memorialized them, cutting away what was troublesome and harmful and recording what hit the mean; he took 731 articles of Zhang Fei's commentary and 791 of Du Yu's, and where the two houses had paired explanations so that the meaning was complete he took another 107 articles; where the commentaries were the same he took 103 articles, gathering them into one book—in all 1,732 articles, in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Zhi, the Secretariat's revising clerk, had drafted a consolidated code and submitted it, stripping burdensome provisions and keeping what was balanced; he drew on 731 glosses by Zhang Fei and 791 by Du Yu, added 107 where both commentators were needed for a full reading, and retained 103 where they agreed—1,732 articles in all, compiled into twenty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 請付外詳校，擿其違謬。

translations.literal: He requested that it be sent outside for detailed collation and that violations and errors be picked out.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the draft be circulated for thorough review so that mistakes could be identified and removed.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented by edict.

sentences.zh: 於是公卿八座參議，考正舊注，有輕重處，竟陵王子良下意多使從輕。

translations.literal: Thereupon the eight excellencies among the nobles and ministers joined in deliberation to examine and correct the old commentaries; where punishments had lighter and heavier readings, Prince Ziliang of Jingling's instructions mostly favored the lighter.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers then met to revise the old annotations; on disputed penalties Prince Ziliang of Jingling usually directed them toward the milder reading.

sentences.zh: 其中朝議不能斷者，則制旨平決。

translations.literal: Among these, what the court deliberation could not decide was settled by the sovereign's express decision.
translations.idiomatic: Where the court could not agree, the emperor's own ruling settled the matter.

sentences.zh: 至九年，珪表上律文二十卷，錄序一卷，又立律學助教，依五經例，詔報從之。

translations.literal: By the ninth year, Gui memorialized and submitted the statutory text in twenty scrolls with a preface in one scroll; he also proposed establishing assistant instructors in penal studies on the model of the Five Classics, and an edict in reply approved this.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Kong Gui presented the code in twenty fascicles with a one-scroll preface and proposed penal-studies instructors on the model of the Five Classics; the throne approved by edict.

sentences.zh: 事竟不行。

translations.literal: In the end the matter was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing came of it in the end.

sentences.zh: 轉御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the post of Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 建武初，為平西長史、南郡太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he was Chief Clerk of the Pacification-West Army and Governor of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianwu era he served as chief clerk on the Pacification-West staff and as governor of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 珪以魏連歲南伐，百姓死傷，乃上表陳通和之策，帝不從。

translations.literal: Gui, because Wei for successive years had marched south to attack and the common people had died and been wounded, thereupon memorialized setting forth a policy of general peace; the emperor did not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Wei had raided the south year after year and the people had suffered heavy losses, Kong Gui submitted a memorial urging peace; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 征侍中，不行，留本任。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary but did not go; he remained in his original post.
translations.idiomatic: He was called to court as Attendant-in-Ordinary but declined to leave his post.

sentences.zh: 珪風韻清疏，好文詠，飲酒七八斗。

translations.literal: Gui's bearing was clear and spare; he loved literary composition and song, and could drink seven or eight dou of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Gui carried himself with airy clarity; he loved poetry and could put away seven or eight dou of wine.

sentences.zh: 與外兄張融情趣相得，又與琅邪王思遠、廬江何點、點弟胤並款交，不樂世務。

translations.literal: With his cousin on his mother's side, Zhang Rong, his temperament matched; moreover with Wang Siyuan of Langye, He Dian of Lujiang, and Dian's younger brother Yin he formed warm friendships, and he took no joy in worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was kindred in spirit with his maternal cousin Zhang Rong, and was on intimate terms with Wang Siyuan of Langye, He Dian of Lujiang, and Dian's brother He Yin—he had little taste for public business.

sentences.zh: 居宅盛營山水，憑几獨酌，傍無雜事。

translations.literal: At his residence he lavishly laid out mountains and waters; leaning on his armrest he drank alone, with no miscellaneous affairs at his side.
translations.idiomatic: His home was landscaped with ponds and rockeries; he would lean on a low table, drink alone, and keep the world at bay.

sentences.zh: 門庭之內，草萊不翦。

translations.literal: Within his gate and courtyard the wild grass was not cut.
translations.idiomatic: He never trimmed the weeds in his courtyard.

sentences.zh: 中有蛙鳴，或問之曰：「欲為陳蕃乎？

translations.literal: Frogs croaked within it; someone asked him, saying, "Do you wish to be like Chen Fan?
translations.idiomatic: Frogs sang in the yard; a visitor asked, "Are you trying to imitate Chen Fan?

sentences.zh: 」珪笑答曰：「我以此當兩部鼓吹，何必效蕃。

translations.literal: " Gui smiled and replied, "I take this as my two-section wind-and-percussion; why must I imitate Fan?
translations.idiomatic: " Kong Gui smiled and said, "I count these as my paired orchestras—why should I copy Fan?

sentences.zh: 」王晏嘗鳴鼓吹候之，聞群蛙鳴，曰：「此殊聒人耳。

translations.literal: " Wang Yan once came with wind-and-percussion bands to call on him; hearing the chorus of frogs, he said, "This is truly grating on the ear.
translations.idiomatic: " Once Wang Yan arrived with a full military band; when he heard the frogs he said, "That racket is unbearable.

sentences.zh: 」珪曰：「我聽鼓吹，殆不及此。

translations.literal: " Gui said, "When I listen to wind music, it hardly equals this.
translations.idiomatic: " Kong Gui replied, "The music I hear from your band scarcely matches this.

sentences.zh: 」晏甚有慚色。

translations.literal: " Yan was deeply ashamed in countenance.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Yan flushed with embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，為都官尚書，遷太子詹事，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan he was Director of the Ministry of Justice, was transferred to Steward of the Heir Apparent, and was given the additional title of Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongyuan he became Director of the Ministry of Justice, then Steward of the Heir Apparent with the additional rank of Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 三年，珪疾，東昏屏除，以床舁之走，因此疾甚，遂卒。

translations.literal: In the third year, Gui fell ill; Emperor Dong Hun carried out a purge, and he was borne away on a bed in flight; because of this his illness grew severe, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Kong Gui fell ill; during Dong Hun's purge he was carried off on a litter in the rout, his condition worsened, and he died.

sentences.zh: 贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.

sentences.zh: 劉懷珍字道玉，平原人，漢膠東康王寄之後也。

translations.literal: Liu Huaizhen, style name Daoyu, was a man of Pingyuan and a descendant of Ji, Prince Kang of Jiaodong of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huaizhen, styled Daoyu, came from Pingyuan and traced his line to Ji, Prince Kang of Jiaodong under the Han.

sentences.zh: 其先劉植為平原太守，因家焉。

translations.literal: His forebear Liu Zhi was Governor of Pingyuan and thereupon made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: An ancestor, Liu Zhi, had been governor of Pingyuan and settled the family in that commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖昶從慕容德南度河，因家于北海都昌。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chang followed Murong De south across the river and thereupon made his home at Duchang in Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chang accompanied Murong De south across the Yellow River and established the clan at Duchang in Beihai.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝平齊，以為青州中從事，位至員外常侍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song pacified Qi, he made him Assistant Investigator of Qing Province; he reached the post of Extraordinary Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Song conquered Qi he appointed him Assistant Investigator of Qing Province; he rose to Extraordinary Attendant.

sentences.zh: 伯父奉伯，宋世位至陳南頓二郡太守。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Fengbo, in the Song dynasty, reached the post of Governor of the two commanderies of Chen and Nandun.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Fengbo had served in Song as governor of both Chen and Nandun.

sentences.zh: 懷珍幼隨奉伯至壽陽，豫州刺史趙伯符出獵，百姓聚觀，懷珍獨避不視，奉伯異之，曰：「此兒方興吾家。

translations.literal: Huaizhen in youth followed Fengbo to Shouyang; the Inspector Zhao Bofu went out hunting, and the common people gathered to watch; Huaizhen alone avoided it and would not look; Fengbo thought it strange and said, "This boy will revive our house.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Liu Huaizhen went with Fengbo to Shouyang; when Inspector Zhao Bofu rode out to hunt and crowds gathered to stare, Huaizhen alone turned away; Fengbo marveled and said, "This child will restore our clan.

sentences.zh: 」本州辟主簿。

translations.literal: " The province summoned him as Registrar.
translations.idiomatic: " The province recruited him as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十八年，亡命司馬順則聚党東陽，州遣懷珍將數千人討平之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia, the outlaw Sima Shunze gathered a party at Dongyang; the province sent Huaizhen to lead several thousand men to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia year 28 the fugitive Sima Shunze raised a band in Dongyang; the province dispatched Huaizhen with several thousand troops to crush the rising.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝問破賊事，懷珍讓功不肯當，親人怪問焉，懷珍曰：「昔國子尼恥陳河間之級，吾豈能論邦域之捷哉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Song asked about the defeat of the bandits; Huaizhen declined merit and would not accept credit; kinsmen wondered and questioned him, and Huaizhen said, "In old times Guo Zini was ashamed to claim the rank of Hejian from Chen; how could I discuss a victory within the realm?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen asked about the campaign, Huaizhen refused to take credit; relatives pressed him, and he said, "Guo Zini once disdained a fief from Chen at Hejian—how could I boast of a provincial victory?

sentences.zh: 」時人稱之。

translations.literal: " Men of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: " His contemporaries admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭出鎮盱眙，道遇懷珍，以應對見重，取為驃騎長史兼墨曹行參軍。

translations.literal: When Prince Jiangxia Yi Gong went out to garrison Xuyi, on the road he met Huaizhen; because of his replies he was esteemed, and he was taken as Chief Clerk of the Cavalry General's staff and Acting Aide in the Ink Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jiangxia went to take up his post at Xuyi he met Huaizhen on the road, was impressed by his conversation, and made him chief clerk on the Cavalry General's staff with a concurrent post in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 孝建初，為義恭大司馬參軍、直合將軍，隨府轉太宰參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojian he was a staff officer to Yi Gong as Grand Marshal and General of the Direct Guard, and followed the prince's establishment when it was transferred to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaojian he served Prince Jiangxia as staff officer and general of the palace guard, and moved with the prince's office when it became the Grand Preceptor's establishment.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，以軍功拜樂陵河間二郡太守，賜爵廣晉縣侯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming, on military merit he was appointed Governor of the two commanderies of Leling and Hejian and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangjin County.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming year 2, for military service he was made governor of Leling and Hejian and enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangjin.

sentences.zh: 司空竟陵王誕反，郡人王弼門族甚盛，勸懷珍起兵助誕，懷珍殺之。

translations.literal: When the Minister of Works, Prince of Jingling, rebelled, a man of the commandery, Wang Bi, whose clan was very powerful, urged Huaizhen to raise troops to aid the prince; Huaizhen killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jingling of Jingling rebelled as Minister of Works, the local magnate Wang Bi pressed Huaizhen to join the revolt; Huaizhen had him executed.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其誠，除豫章王子尚車騎參軍，母憂去職。

translations.literal: The emperor commended his loyalty and appointed him Cavalry Aide to the Prince of Yuzhang, Zi Shang; he left office on his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his fidelity and made him cavalry aide to Prince Yuzhang Zi Shang; he then resigned to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，見江夏王義恭，義恭曰：「別子多年，那得不老？

translations.literal: When mourning ended he saw Prince Jiangxia Yi Gong; Yi Gong said, "We have been apart many years—how can you not be old?
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he visited Prince Jiangxia, who said, "We have not met in years—surely you must have aged?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「公恩未報，何敢便老。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Your grace's favor is not yet repaid—how dare I already be old?
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "I have not yet repaid Your Highness's kindness—how dare I claim to be old?

sentences.zh: 」義恭善其對。

translations.literal: " Yi Gong approved his reply.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince was pleased with his answer.

sentences.zh: 累遷黃門郎，領虎賁中郎將。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Yellow Gate Attendant and concurrently commanded the Tiger Guard as General of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Yellow Gate Attendant and also led the Tiger Guard as general of the household.

sentences.zh: 桂陽王休範反，加懷珍前將軍，守石頭。

translations.literal: When Prince Guiyang Xiufan rebelled, Huaizhen was given the additional title of General of the Van and defended Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Guiyang rebelled, Huaizhen was made General of the Van and held Shitou fortress.

sentences.zh: 出為豫州刺史，加督。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Yu Province, with the additional title of Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as inspector of Yu Province with supervisory authority.

sentences.zh: 建平王景素反，懷珍遣子靈哲領兵赴建鄴。

translations.literal: When Prince Jianping Jingsu rebelled, Huaizhen sent his son Lingzhe to lead troops to hurry to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jianping rebelled, Huaizhen dispatched his son Lingzhe at the head of troops to relieve Jianye.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之在荊楚，遣使人許天保說結懷珍，斬之，送首于齊高帝，封中宿縣侯，進平南將軍，增督二州。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi was in Jing and Chu; he sent a man, Xu Tianbao, to persuade and win over Huaizhen; Huaizhen beheaded him, sent the head to Emperor Gao of Qi, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhongsu County, was advanced to General Who Pacifies the South, and had his supervisory authority increased by two provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi, holding Jing and Chu, sent Xu Tianbao to win Huaizhen over; Huaizhen executed the envoy, sent his head to the future Emperor Gao of Qi, and was made Marquis of Zhongsu, promoted to General Who Pacifies the South with authority over two additional provinces.

sentences.zh: 初，宋孝武世，齊高帝為舍人，懷珍為直合，相遇早舊。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the era of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, Emperor Gao of Qi was a Palace Attendant and Huaizhen was in the Direct Guard; they met early and were old acquaintances.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, in Emperor Xiaowu's reign, the future Emperor Gao had been a palace attendant and Huaizhen a guard officer—they had known each other since youth.

sentences.zh: 懷珍假還青州，高帝有白驄馬，齧人，不可騎，送與懷珍別。

translations.literal: When Huaizhen took leave to return to Qing Province, the emperor had a white piebald horse that bit people and could not be ridden; he sent it to Huaizhen as a parting gift.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaizhen went home on leave to Qing Province, the future emperor gave him a white piebald stallion that bit and could not be ridden, sending it as a farewell gift.

sentences.zh: 懷珍報上百匹絹。

translations.literal: Huaizhen sent back a hundred bolts of silk in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen returned the courtesy with a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 或謂懷珍曰：「蕭公此馬不中騎，是以與君耳。

translations.literal: Someone said to Huaizhen, "Lord Xiao's horse is unfit to ride; that is why he gave it to you.
translations.idiomatic: Someone told him, "Lord Xiao's horse is unrideable—that is why he palmed it off on you.

sentences.zh: 君報百匹，不亦多乎？

translations.literal: Yet you sent back a hundred bolts—is that not too much?
translations.idiomatic: A hundred bolts in return—is that not excessive?

sentences.zh: 」懷珍曰：「蕭君局量堂堂，甯應負人此絹。

translations.literal: " Huaizhen said, "Lord Xiao's breadth of mind is imposing; how could he begrudge a man this silk?
translations.idiomatic: " Huaizhen said, "Lord Xiao's magnanimity is vast—surely he would not stint at this silk.

sentences.zh: 吾方欲以身名托之，豈計錢物多少。」

translations.literal: I am just about to entrust my person and name to him—how could I reckon the amount of money and goods?"
translations.idiomatic: I mean to stake my life and reputation on him—why should I haggle over trifles?"

sentences.zh: 高帝輔政，以懷珍內資未多，徵為都官尚書，領前將軍。

translations.literal: When the emperor served as regent, because Huaizhen's resources within the court were not yet abundant, he summoned him as Director of the Ministry of Justice and concurrently General of the Van.
translations.idiomatic: Once the future emperor became regent, deeming Huaizhen's influence at court still thin, he recalled him as Director of the Ministry of Justice with the concurrent rank of General of the Van.

sentences.zh: 以第四子晃代為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He made his fourth son Huang replace him as Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed his fourth son Huang to succeed him as inspector of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 或疑懷珍不受代，高帝曰：「我布衣時，懷珍便推懷投款，況在今日，寧當有異。

translations.literal: Some suspected that Huaizhen would not accept replacement; the emperor said, "When I was still in plain cloth, Huaizhen already opened his heart and pledged loyalty—how much more so today; how could he act differently?
translations.idiomatic: Some doubted that Huaizhen would yield his post; the regent said, "Even when I wore homespun, Huaizhen gave me his wholehearted allegiance—will he change now?

sentences.zh: 」晃發經日，疑論不止，上乃遣軍主房靈人領百騎進送晃。

translations.literal: " After Huang had set out for several days, the doubting talk did not cease; the sovereign thereupon sent the army commander Fang Lingren at the head of a hundred horsemen to escort Huang forward.
translations.idiomatic: " Huang had been on the road for days and rumors still swirled, so the regent sent the commander Fang Lingren with a hundred cavalry to escort the new inspector.

sentences.zh: 謂靈人曰：「論者謂懷珍必有異同，我期之有素，必不應爾。

translations.literal: He told Lingren, "The talkers say Huaizhen is sure to disagree; I have long expected otherwise—he surely will not act so.
translations.idiomatic: He told Fang Lingren, "People insist Huaizhen will resist—but I have known him too long; he will not.

sentences.zh: 卿是其鄉里，故遣卿行，非唯衛新，亦以迎故。

translations.literal: You are his fellow townsman; therefore I send you on this mission—not only to guard the new man, but also to welcome the old.
translations.idiomatic: You are from his home district; I send you not only to protect the newcomer but to bring the old man back in honor.

sentences.zh: 」懷珍還，乃授相國右司馬。

translations.literal: " When Huaizhen returned, he was then appointed Right Chief Clerk of the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: " When Huaizhen came in, he was made Right Chief Clerk to the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 懷珍年老，以禁旅辛勤，求為閒職，轉光祿大夫，卒。

translations.literal: Huaizhen was old; because service in the palace guard was toilsome, he requested a leisurely post, was transferred to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the strain of palace duty wearied him; he asked for a quieter post, was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and died.

sentences.zh: 遺言薄葬。

translations.literal: His testamentary words were for a plain burial.
translations.idiomatic: He left instructions to be buried simply.

sentences.zh: 贈雍州刺史，諡敬侯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Inspector of Yong Province, with the posthumous title Marquis Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made inspector of Yong Province and given the posthumous title Marquis Jing.

sentences.zh: 子靈哲字文明，位齊郡太守、前軍將軍。

translations.literal: His son Lingzhe, style name Wenming, held the posts of Governor of Qi Commandery and General of the Forward Army.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Lingzhe, styled Wenming, served as governor of Qi Commandery and General of the Forward Army.

sentences.zh: 靈哲所生母嘗病，靈哲躬自祈禱，夢見黃衣老公與藥曰：「可取此食之，疾立可愈。

translations.literal: When Lingzhe's birth mother once fell ill, Lingzhe personally prayed; he dreamed of a yellow-robed old man who gave him medicine, saying, "Take this and eat it; the illness will immediately be cured.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingzhe's own mother fell ill he prayed in person; in a dream a yellow-robed old man handed him medicine, saying, "Eat this and she will recover at once.

sentences.zh: 」靈哲驚覺，於枕間得之，如言而疾愈。

translations.literal: " Startled awake, he found it between his pillows; as spoken, the illness was cured.
translations.idiomatic: " He woke with a start and found the drug beside his pillow; he gave it to her, and she was healed as promised.

sentences.zh: 藥似竹根，於齋前種，葉似鳧茈。

translations.literal: The medicine resembled bamboo root; he planted it before the fasting hall, and the leaves resembled water caltrop.
translations.idiomatic: The herb looked like bamboo root; he planted it before his oratory, and its leaves resembled water caltrop.

sentences.zh: 嫡母崔氏及兄子景煥，泰始中為魏所獲。

translations.literal: His father's principal wife, the Lady Cui, and his elder brother's son Jinghuan, in the Taishi era were captured by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father's principal wife, Lady Cui, and his elder brother's son Jinghuan had been taken captive by Wei in the Taishi period.

sentences.zh: 靈哲為布衣，不聽樂。

translations.literal: Lingzhe, as a commoner, would not listen to music.
translations.idiomatic: While still a private gentleman, Lingzhe refused all music.

sentences.zh: 及懷珍卒，當襲爵，靈哲固辭，以兄子在魏，存亡未測，無容越當茅土。

translations.literal: When Huaizhen died, he was due to inherit the enfeoffment; Lingzhe firmly declined, on the ground that his elder brother's son was in Wei and whether he lived or died was not yet known—he could not leap ahead to take the fief.
translations.idiomatic: At Huaizhen's death the title should have passed to him, but Lingzhe refused, saying his nephew was still in Wei and might be alive—he could not seize the marquisate ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷義之。

translations.literal: The court approved his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The court honored his conduct.

sentences.zh: 靈哲傾產贖嫡母及景煥，累年不能得。

translations.literal: Lingzhe exhausted his property to ransom the principal wife and Jinghuan, but for years could not obtain them.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his entire fortune trying to ransom Lady Cui and Jinghuan, yet year after year failed to bring them home.

sentences.zh: 武帝哀之，令北使者請之，魏人送以還南，襲懷珍封爵。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu pitied him, ordered the northern envoy to request them, and the men of Wei sent them back south; he then inherited Huaizhen's enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang took pity and had his envoy to the north demand their release; Wei returned them, and only then did Lingzhe accept his father's title.

sentences.zh: 靈哲位兗州刺史，隆昌元年卒。

translations.literal: Lingzhe held the post of Inspector of Yan Province and died in the first year of Longchang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to inspector of Yan Province and died in the first year of Longchang.

sentences.zh: 峻字孝標，本名法武，懷珍從父弟也。

translations.literal: Jun, style name Xiaobiao, original name Fawu, was Huaizhen's younger cousin on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun, styled Xiaobiao—born Fawu—was Huaizhen's younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 父琁之，仕宋為始興內史。

translations.literal: His father Xuanzhi served the Song as Administrator of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Xuanzhi held office under the Liu Song as inner governor of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 峻生期月而琁之卒，其母許氏攜峻及其兄法鳳還鄉里。

translations.literal: Jun was one month old when Xuanzhi died; his mother, Lady Xu, took Jun and his elder brother Fafeng back to their native place.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun was barely a month old when his father died; Lady Xu brought the infant and his elder brother Fafeng home to their clan seat.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始初，魏克青州，峻時年八歲，為人所略為奴至中山。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song Taishi era, Wei conquered Qing Province; Jun was then eight years old and was seized by others, carried off as a slave to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Taishi years of the Song, when the Northern Wei took Qingzhou, eight-year-old Liu Jun was captured and sold as a slave in Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 中山富人劉寶湣峻，以束帛贖之，教以書學。

translations.literal: Liu Bao, a rich man of Zhongshan, pitied Jun, redeemed him with a bundle of silk, and instructed him in letters and learning.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy Zhongshan patron named Liu Bao took pity on him, bought him back with silk gifts, and taught him to read and write.

sentences.zh: 魏人聞其江南有戚屬，更徙之代都。

translations.literal: The Wei people heard that he had kinsmen south of the Yangtze and moved him again to the capital of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that he had relatives in the south, the northerners transferred him to the Wei capital at Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 居貧不自立，與母並出家為尼僧，既而還俗。

translations.literal: Living in poverty and unable to support himself, he and his mother together left the world to become Buddhist nuns, and afterward returned to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to sustain themselves, mother and son briefly took monastic vows as nuns, then returned to secular life.

sentences.zh: 峻好學，寄人廡下，自課讀書，常燎麻炬，從夕達旦。

translations.literal: Jun loved learning; he lodged under another's eaves, set himself lessons in reading, and often burned hemp torches from evening until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun was consumed by study. Lodging in a borrowed lean-to, he drove himself through the texts, keeping hemp torches alight from dusk to daybreak.

sentences.zh: 時或昏睡，爇其鬚髮，及覺復讀，其精力如此。

translations.literal: At times when he grew drowsy, he would burn his beard and hair, and when he awoke would read again—such was his fervor.
translations.idiomatic: When sleep threatened, he singed his own beard and hair to wake himself, then returned to the books with that fierce discipline.

sentences.zh: 時魏孝文選盡物望，江南人士才學之徒，咸見申擢，峻兄弟不蒙選拔。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaowen of Wei selected all men of public esteem; scholars and talented men from the lands south of the Yangtze were all promoted and elevated, but Jun and his brother were not chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of the Northern Wei was recruiting every celebrated talent from the Jiangnan elite, yet neither Liu Jun nor his brother was selected.

sentences.zh: 齊永明中，俱奔江南，更改名峻字孝標。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era of Qi they both fled south to the Yangtze region and changed his name to Jun, style name Xiaobiao.
translations.idiomatic: During Qi Yongming they escaped south together; he took the name Jun and the style Xiaobiao—Liu Jun as the world would know him.

sentences.zh: 自以少時未開悟，晚更厲精，明慧過人。

translations.literal: He considered that in youth he had not been enlightened, but in later years he applied himself with greater intensity, and his clarity surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: He felt he had been slow to awaken as a youth, yet in maturity redoubled his effort until his brilliance outshone his peers.

sentences.zh: 苦所見不博，聞有異書，必往祈借。

translations.literal: He grieved that what he had seen was not broad; hearing of a rare book, he would always go to pray and borrow it.
translations.idiomatic: Distressed by the narrowness of what he had read, he would track down any unusual text he heard of and go plead to borrow it.

sentences.zh: 清河崔慰祖謂之「書淫」。

translations.literal: Cui Weizu of Qinghe called him "book lecher."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Weizu of Qinghe dubbed him "an addict of books."

sentences.zh: 於是博極群書，文藻秀出。

translations.literal: Thereupon he read exhaustively through all books, and his literary adornments stood forth outstandingly.
translations.idiomatic: In time he mastered an immense library, and his prose rose luminous above the common run.

sentences.zh: 故其自序云：「黌中濟濟皆升堂，亦有愚者解衣裳。

translations.literal: Therefore in his autobiographical preface he said, "In the school courtyard all in their throngs ascend the hall, yet there are also dullards who undress their robes.
translations.idiomatic: In his autobiographical preface he wrote, "In the academy the crowd all climb to the hall, yet fools there are who only strip off their robes.

sentences.zh: 」言其少年魯鈍也。

translations.literal: " He spoke of his obtuse youth.
translations.idiomatic: "—a barbed remark on how slow-witted he had been as a boy.

sentences.zh: 時竟陵王子良招學士，峻因人求為子良國職。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Jingling, Ziliang, recruited scholars; Jun through another person requested to become a member of Ziliang's prince's household staff.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, was gathering literati, Liu Jun had an intermediary seek a post on the prince's staff.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書徐孝嗣抑而不許，用為南海王侍郎，不就。

translations.literal: Xu Xiaosi, Minister of the Civil Service, suppressed the request and would not permit it, and instead appointed him Gentleman-Attendant to the Prince of Nanhai, but he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Civil Service Xu Xiaosi blocked the appointment and offered him instead a post as gentleman-attendant to the Prince of Nanhai—which Liu Jun declined.

sentences.zh: 至齊明帝時，蕭遙欣為豫州，引為府刑獄，禮遇甚厚。

translations.literal: When it came to Emperor Ming of Qi, Xiao Yaoqin was Inspector of Yu Province and brought him in as prison officer of the headquarters, treating him with very great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming of Qi, when Xiao Yaoqin governed Yuzhou, Liu Jun entered his staff as prisons officer and was honored with exceptional generosity.

sentences.zh: 遙欣尋卒，久不調。

translations.literal: Yaoqin soon died, and for a long time he received no appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoqin died not long after, and Liu Jun went years without another office.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，召入西省，與學士賀蹤典校秘閣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian of Liang he was summoned into the Western Bureau and, together with the scholar He Zong, supervised collation in the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: In the opening years of Liang Tianjian he was called to the Western Bureau to catalogue the Secret Archive alongside the academician He Zong.

sentences.zh: 峻兄孝慶時為青州刺史，峻請假省之，坐私載禁物，為有司所奏免官。

translations.literal: Jun's elder brother Xiaoqing was then Inspector of Qing Province; Jun asked leave to visit him, but on account of privately transporting prohibited goods was impeached by the authorities and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Liu Xiaoqing was governor of Qingzhou, and Liu Jun sought leave to visit him; he was impeached for smuggling contraband and stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 安成王秀雅重峻，及安成王遷荊州，引為戶曹參軍，給其書籍，使撰類苑。

translations.literal: Prince An of Cheng, Xiu, greatly esteemed Jun, and when Prince An moved to Jing Province he brought him in as Registrar of the Household Section, supplied him with books, and had him compile the Classified Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiu of Ancheng, who valued him deeply, took him to Jingzhou as registrar in the household bureau, furnished a library, and commissioned the Classified Garden.

sentences.zh: 未及成，復以疾去，因游東陽紫岩山，築室居焉。

translations.literal: Before it was finished he again left on account of illness, and thereupon traveled to Purple Cliff Mountain in Dongyang, built a dwelling, and lived there.
translations.idiomatic: The work was unfinished when illness drove him away; he wandered to Purple Cliff in Dongyang, built a house, and settled among the peaks.

sentences.zh: 為山棲志，其文甚美。

translations.literal: He wrote A Record of Dwelling in the Mountains, and its prose was very beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: He composed "Mind of a Mountain Dweller," a piece of prose celebrated for its beauty.

sentences.zh: 初，梁武帝招文學之士，有高才者多被引進，擢以不次。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Wu of Liang recruited men of letters; those of high talent were mostly brought in and promoted out of regular order.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, Emperor Wu of Liang courted literary talent, advancing the gifted with extraordinary rapidity.

sentences.zh: 峻率性而動，不能隨眾沈浮。

translations.literal: Jun acted according to his nature and could not follow the crowd in sinking or floating.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun followed his own temperament and would not bob with the courtly tide.

sentences.zh: 武帝每集文士策經史事，時范雲、沈約之徒皆引短推長，帝乃悅，加其賞賚。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor gathered literati to examine them on events from the classics and histories, at that time Fan Yun, Shen Yue, and their sort all cited their weaknesses and praised their strengths; the emperor was then pleased and increased their rewards.
translations.idiomatic: At the emperor's symposiums on classical and historical questions, Fan Yun, Shen Yue, and the rest professed modesty while steering answers to their strengths; the emperor was delighted and heaped gifts upon them.

sentences.zh: 會策錦被事，咸言已罄，帝試呼問峻，峻時貧悴冗散，忽請紙筆，疏十餘事，坐客皆驚，帝不覺失色。

translations.literal: Once when they were examined on the affair of the brocade quilt, all said it was exhausted; the emperor tried calling upon Jun to ask; Jun was then poor, haggard, and idly dispersed; suddenly he requested paper and brush and set forth more than ten matters; all seated guests were startled, and the emperor involuntarily changed color.
translations.idiomatic: Once the topic turned to the brocade-quilt affair and everyone declared the sources exhausted, the emperor called on the shabby, neglected Liu Jun; he asked abruptly for brush and paper and listed more than a dozen points, astonishing the assembly and bringing a flush of dismay to the throne.

sentences.zh: 自是惡之，不復引見。

translations.literal: From this he came to dislike him and no longer summoned him to audiences.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the emperor disliked him and never summoned him again.

sentences.zh: 及峻類苑成，凡一百二十卷，帝即命諸學士撰華林遍略以高之，竟不見用。

translations.literal: When Jun's Classified Garden was completed, in all one hundred twenty scrolls, the emperor forthwith commanded the various scholars to compile the Comprehensive Outline of the Flourishing Grove to surpass it, but in the end it was not used.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jun's 120-juan Classified Garden was finished, the emperor ordered a rival compendium, the Comprehensive Outline of the Flourishing Grove, yet Liu Jun's work was never adopted.

sentences.zh: 乃著辯命論以寄其懷。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wrote "Discourse on Fate" to lodge his feelings.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote his "Discourse on Fate" to voice what he carried in his heart.

sentences.zh: 論成，中山劉沼致書以難之，凡再反，峻並為申析以答之。

translations.literal: When the discourse was complete, Liu Zhao of Zhongshan sent a letter to challenge it, in all twice back and forth, and Jun for each wrote analyses in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao of Zhongshan wrote twice to dispute the treatise, and Liu Jun answered each exchange with careful refutation.

sentences.zh: 會沼卒，不見峻後報者，峻乃為書以序其事。

translations.literal: When Zhao happened to die, he did not see Jun's later replies; Jun thereupon wrote a letter to narrate the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao died before the final rejoinders could reach him, so Liu Jun composed a letter setting out how the debate had stood.

sentences.zh: 其文論並多不載。

translations.literal: His essays and treatises for the most part are not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his essays and disputations are omitted from this record.

sentences.zh: 峻又嘗為自序，其略云：

translations.literal: Jun also once wrote an autobiographical preface, its gist saying:
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun also drafted an autobiographical preface, which in brief runs:

sentences.zh: 余自比馮敬通，而有同之者三，異之者四。

translations.literal: I have compared myself to Feng Jingtong, and there are three points of likeness and four of difference.
translations.idiomatic: I have likened myself to Feng Jingtong, noting three resemblances and four divergences.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 敬通雄才冠世，志剛金石；

translations.literal: Jingtong's heroic talent crowned the age, and his resolve was hard as metal and stone;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jingtong's genius towered over his age, his will firm as bronze and stone;

sentences.zh: 餘雖不及之，而節亮慷慨。
