translations.literal: I, though I do not reach him, yet have integrity bright and open-hearted generosity.
translations.idiomatic: I fall short of him, yet my integrity is bright and my spirit generous.

sentences.zh: 此一同也。

translations.literal: This is the first likeness.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first point of likeness.

sentences.zh: 敬通逢中興明君，而終不試用；

translations.literal: Jingtong met an enlightened ruler at the restoration, yet in the end was never employed;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jingtong lived under a restoring sage ruler, yet never won office;

sentences.zh: 余逢命世英主，亦擯斥當年。

translations.literal: I have met a heroic lord of a destined age, yet was also cast out in that same year.
translations.idiomatic: I too have met an age-shaping sovereign, yet was driven off in his prime.

sentences.zh: 此二同也。

translations.literal: This is the second likeness.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second resemblance.

sentences.zh: 敬通有忌妻，至於身操井臼；

translations.literal: Jingtong had a jealous wife, so that he himself worked the well and mortar;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jingtong had a jealous wife and came to haul water and grind grain himself;

sentences.zh: 餘有悍室，亦令家道轗軻。

translations.literal: I have a fierce wife, and she too has made the household path rough and stony.
translations.idiomatic: I have a shrewish spouse who has likewise wrecked the fortunes of our house.

sentences.zh: 此三同也。

translations.literal: This is the third likeness.
translations.idiomatic: That is the third parallel.

sentences.zh: 敬通當更始世，手握兵符，躍馬肉食；

translations.literal: Jingtong in the era of Gengshi held the military tally in his hand, leaped on horses and ate meat;
translations.idiomatic: In the Gengshi years Feng Jingtong held command, rode at the hunt, and feasted on meat;

sentences.zh: 餘自少迄長，戚戚無歡。

translations.literal: I from youth to old age have been sorrowful without joy.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood to gray hairs I have known only grief, never cheer.

sentences.zh: 此一異也。

translations.literal: This is the first difference.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first contrast.

sentences.zh: 敬通有子仲文，官成名立；

translations.literal: Jingtong had a son Zhongwen, who in office achieved fame and established his name;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jingtong's son Zhongwen rose in office and won renown;

sentences.zh: 餘禍同伯道，永無血胤。

translations.literal: My misfortune is the same as that of Bo Dao; forever without a blood heir.
translations.idiomatic: My sorrow matches that of Bo Dao—I have no descendant to carry my line.

sentences.zh: 此二異也。

translations.literal: This is the second difference.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second divergence.

sentences.zh: 敬通膂力剛強，老而益壯；

translations.literal: Jingtong's physical strength was firm and strong, and in old age he grew still more robust;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jingtong's thews were iron, and he grew stronger in age;

sentences.zh: 餘有犬馬之疾，溘死無時。

translations.literal: I have the sickness of dogs and horses and may die suddenly at any time.
translations.idiomatic: I am ill with a wasting malady and may drop dead at any hour.

sentences.zh: 此三異也。

translations.literal: This is the third difference.
translations.idiomatic: That is the third point of difference.

sentences.zh: 敬通雖芝殘蕙焚，終填溝壑，而為名賢所慕，其風流郁烈芬芳，久而彌盛；

translations.literal: Though Jingtong's orchid was broken and his sweet-flag burned, he in the end filled a ditch and gully, yet was admired by famous worthies; his manners were lush, fierce, and fragrant, and after long time grow still more abundant;
translations.idiomatic: Though Feng Jingtong died obscure, reviled orchids and burnt sweet-flag, the eminent still cherished his memory, and his renown grows fuller with the years;

sentences.zh: 余聲塵寂莫，世不吾知，魂魄一去，將同秋草。

translations.literal: My voice and dust are silent and still; the world does not know me; when soul and spirit depart once, I shall be the same as autumn grasses.
translations.idiomatic: My name falls silent, the world ignores me, and when my soul leaves it will moulder like autumn grass.

sentences.zh: 此四異也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth difference.
translations.idiomatic: That is the fourth contrast.

sentences.zh: 所以力自為序，遺之好事云。

translations.literal: For this reason I have striven to write the preface myself and bequeath it to lovers of fine things, so they say.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I wrote this preface myself and leave it for those who delight in such things.

sentences.zh: 峻本將門，兄法鳳自北歸，改名孝慶字仲昌。

translations.literal: Jun's family was originally of a military house; his elder brother Fafeng returned from the north, changed his name to Xiaoqing, style name Zhongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun came from a martial clan; his brother Fafeng, returning from the north, took the name Xiaoqing, styled Zhongchang.

sentences.zh: 早有幹略，齊末為兗州刺史，舉兵應梁武，封餘幹男，曆官顯重。

translations.literal: In early life he had capacity and strategy; at the end of Qi he was Inspector of Yan Province, raised troops to respond to Emperor Wu of Liang, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yugan, and passed through offices of manifest weight.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted early with grit and strategy, he governed Yanzhou at the end of Qi, rallied to Emperor Wu of Liang, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yugan, and rose to eminent posts.

sentences.zh: 峻獨篤志好學，居東陽，吳、會人士多從其學。

translations.literal: Jun alone had a steadfast will and loved learning; dwelling in Dongyang, men of Wu and Guiji for the most part followed him in study.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun alone clung to scholarship; living in Dongyang, he drew students from across the Wu and Kuaiji regions.

sentences.zh: 普通三年卒，年六十。

translations.literal: In the third year of Putong he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Putong year 3, at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 門人諡曰玄靖先生。

translations.literal: His disciples gave him the posthumous title Master Xuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His students honored him posthumously as Master Xuanjing.

sentences.zh: 劉沼字明信，中山魏昌人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhao, style name Mingxin, was a man of Weichang in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao, styled Mingxin, came from Weichang in Zhongshan commandery.

sentences.zh: 六世祖輿，晉驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Yu was General of Agile Cavalry of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Yu had served the Jin as General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 沼幼善屬文，及長博學，位終秣陵令。

translations.literal: Zhao in youth was skilled at composing prose; when grown he was broadly learned; his office ended as Magistrate of Moling.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote well from childhood and became a wide-ranging scholar, ending his career as magistrate of Moling.

sentences.zh: 懷慰字彥泰，懷珍從子也。

translations.literal: Huaiwei, style name Yantai, was Huaizhen's nephew on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huaiwei, styled Yantai, was Liu Huaizhen's nephew.

sentences.zh: 祖奉伯，宋元嘉中為冠軍長史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fengbo in the Yuanjia era of Song served as Chief Clerk to the Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fengbo served as chief clerk to the Champion General under Song Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 父乘人，冀州刺史，死于義嘉事。

translations.literal: His father Chengren was Inspector of Ji Province and died in the Yijia affair.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengren, governor of Jizhou, died in the troubles of the Yijia era.

sentences.zh: 懷慰持喪不食醯醬，冬日不用絮衣，養孤弟妹，事寡叔母，皆有恩義。

translations.literal: Huaiwei observed mourning and did not eat pickles and sauces; in winter he did not use padded garments; he raised orphaned younger brothers and sisters and served his widowed uncle's wife—all with kindness and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he refused pickled foods, went winter without padded clothing, raised his orphaned siblings, and cared for his widowed aunt—all with exemplary devotion.

sentences.zh: 仕宋為尚書駕部郎。

translations.literal: He served the Song as Director of the Imperial Carriage Department in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song he served as Director of the Imperial Carriage Department.

sentences.zh: 懷慰宗從善明等為齊高帝心腹，懷慰亦預焉。

translations.literal: Huaiwei's clansmen Shanming and others were the trusted intimates of Emperor Gao of Qi, and Huaiwei also took part therein.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsmen Shanming and others were Emperor Gao of Qi's inner circle, and Liu Huaiwei shared in that trust.

sentences.zh: 齊國建，上欲置齊郡於都下。

translations.literal: When the state of Qi was established, the sovereign wished to place Qi Commandery beneath the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi state was founded, the emperor wished to seat Qi commandery at the capital.

sentences.zh: 議者以江右土沃，流人所歸，乃置於瓜步，以懷慰為輔國將軍、齊郡太守。

translations.literal: The councillors held that the lands east of the Yangtze were fertile and that displaced persons would congregate there, so they placed it at Guabu and made Huaiwei General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Qi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers argued that the rich lands east of the Yangtze would draw refugees, so the seat was set at Guabu and Liu Huaiwei made General Who Assists the State and governor of Qi commandery.

sentences.zh: 上謂懷慰曰：「齊邦是王業所基，吾方欲以為顯任，經理之事，一以委卿。

translations.literal: The sovereign said to Huaiwei, "The state of Qi is the foundation of our royal enterprise; I am just now about to make it a prominent charge, and matters of management I wholly entrust to you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Liu Huaiwei, "Qi is the cradle of our throne; I mean to give you a post of real consequence, and I entrust its entire administration to you.

sentences.zh: 」又手敕曰：「有文事必有武備，今賜卿玉環刀一口。」

translations.literal: " He also wrote a personal edict saying, "Where there are civil affairs there must also be military preparation; now I bestow upon you one jade-ring knife."
translations.idiomatic: " He added a personal directive: "Civil rule demands martial readiness—here is a jade-ring blade for you."

sentences.zh: 懷慰至郡，修城郭，安集居人，墾廢田二百頃，決沈湖灌溉。

translations.literal: When Huaiwei reached the commandery he repaired walls and moats, settled and gathered the inhabitants, opened two hundred qing of abandoned fields, and opened Shen Lake for irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: At his post he rebuilt the walls, resettled the people, reclaimed two hundred qing of fallow land, and cut canals from Shen Lake for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 不受禮謁，人有餉其新米一斛者，懷慰出所食麥飯示之曰：「食有餘，幸不煩此。

translations.literal: He did not accept gifts or calls of ceremony; when someone presented him one hu of new rice, Huaiwei brought out the wheat meal he himself ate and showed it, saying, "My food has surplus; fortunately you need not trouble yourself with this.
translations.idiomatic: He refused gifts and courtesy visits; when a man offered a hu of new rice, Liu Huaiwei set out his own barley meal and said, "I already have enough—please spare yourself the trouble.

sentences.zh: 」因著廉吏論以達其意。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he wrote "Discourse on Incorrupt Officials" to express his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: " He then wrote his "Discourse on Incorrupt Officials" to make his principle plain.

sentences.zh: 高帝聞之，手敕褒賞。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao heard of it and personally edicted commendation and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao heard and sent a personal edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 進督秦、沛二郡，妻子在都，賜米三百石。

translations.literal: He was advanced to oversee Qin and Pei commanderies; his wife and children were in the capital, and he was granted three hundred shi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervise Qin and Pei commanderies; his family remained in the capital and received three hundred shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史柳世隆與懷慰書曰：「膠東流化，潁川致美，以今方古，曾何足云。」

translations.literal: Liu Shilong, Inspector of Yan Province, wrote to Huaiwei saying, "In Jiaodong culture flowed outward; in Yingchuan beauty was brought forth—comparing the present to antiquity, how could it even be spoken of?"
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Liu Shilong of Yanzhou wrote him, "Jiaodong once transformed its people and Yingchuan once perfected its governance—what you have done beside those examples needs no modesty."

sentences.zh: 懷慰本名聞慰，武帝即位，以與舅氏名同，敕改之。

translations.literal: Huaiwei's original name was Wenwei; when Emperor Wu took the throne, because it was the same as his maternal uncle's name, an edict changed it.
translations.idiomatic: Born Wenwei, he was renamed by imperial order when Emperor Wu took the throne because the name matched that of the emperor's uncle.

sentences.zh: 後兼安陸王北中郎司馬，卒。

translations.literal: Later he concurrently served as North Central Army Major to the Prince of Anlu and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later served concurrently as North Central Army major under the Prince of Anlu, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，謂僕射徐孝嗣曰：「劉懷慰若在，朝廷不憂無清吏也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne he said to Vice Director Xu Xiaosi, "If Liu Huaiwei were still alive, the court would not worry over lacking incorrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming succeeded, he told Vice Director Xu Xiaosi, "Had Liu Huaiwei lived, the court would never lack honest officials.

sentences.zh: 」子霽、杳、歊。

translations.literal: " His sons Ji, Yao, and Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: " His sons were Ji, Yao, and Xiao.

sentences.zh: 霽字士湮，九歲能誦左氏傳。

translations.literal: Ji, style name Shiyan, at nine years could recite the Zuo Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji, styled Shiyan, could recite the Zuo Tradition at nine.

sentences.zh: 十四居父憂，有至性，每哭輒嘔血。

translations.literal: At fourteen he was in mourning for his father, had utmost nature, and whenever he wept would vomit blood.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen, mourning his father, he showed such filial depth that weeping brought up blood.

sentences.zh: 家貧，與弟杳、歊勵志勤學。

translations.literal: The family was poor; with his younger brothers Yao and Xiao he spurred their wills and studied diligently.
translations.idiomatic: The household was poor, yet he and his brothers Yao and Xiao drove one another through relentless study.

sentences.zh: 及長，博涉多通。

translations.literal: When grown he broadly traversed many subjects and was thoroughly versed.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood, he ranged widely and mastered much.

sentences.zh: 梁天監中，歷位西昌相，尚書主客侍郎，海鹽令。

translations.literal: In the Tianjian era of Liang he successively held the posts of Chancellor of Xichang, Gentleman-Attendant of the Hosts in the Ministry of Works, and Magistrate of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang Tianjian he served as chancellor of Xichang, gentleman-attendant for guests in the Ministry of Works, and magistrate of Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 霽前後宰二邑，並以和理稱。

translations.literal: Ji before and after governed two districts and in both was praised for harmonious governance.
translations.idiomatic: In two districts he governed, and both knew him for humane, orderly rule.

sentences.zh: 後除建康令，不拜。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Magistrate of Jiankang but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Later offered the magistracy of Jiankang, he declined.

sentences.zh: 母明氏寢疾，霽年已五十，衣不解帶者七旬，誦觀世音經數萬遍。

translations.literal: When his mother, Lady Ming, lay ill, Ji was already fifty years old; for seventy days he did not undo his belt on his garments, and recited the Scripture of Guanyin tens of thousands of times.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Ming fell ill Liu Ji was fifty; for seventy days he never left her side or loosened his belt, and he chanted the Lotus Sutra of Guanyin tens of thousands of times.

sentences.zh: 夜中感夢，見一僧謂曰：「夫人算盡，君精誠篤志，當相為申延。

translations.literal: In the middle of the night he was moved in a dream and saw a monk who said to him, "Your mother's allotted span is exhausted; your sincerity and steadfast will—[I] shall on your behalf petition to extend it.
translations.idiomatic: One night he dreamed a monk who said, "Your mother's term is spent, but your devotion is so deep that I shall plead to prolong her life.

sentences.zh: 」後六十餘日乃亡。

translations.literal: " After more than sixty days she then died.
translations.idiomatic: " She lived a little more than sixty days before she died.

sentences.zh: 霽廬於墓，哀慟過禮，常有雙白鶴循翔廬側，處士阮孝緒致書抑譬焉。

translations.literal: Ji built a hut at the tomb; his grief and lament exceeded the rites; there were often paired white cranes circling and soaring beside the hut; the recluse Ruan Xiaoxu sent a letter to check and admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: He kept mourning huts by the grave, grieving beyond the prescribed rites; a pair of white cranes often circled his shelter, until the recluse Ruan Xiaoxu wrote urging restraint.

sentences.zh: 霽思慕不已，未終喪而卒。

translations.literal: Ji thought of and longed for her without cease and before the mourning was finished died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji could not shake his sorrow and died before the mourning term was complete.

sentences.zh: 著釋俗語八卷，文集十卷。

translations.literal: He authored Explication of Common Sayings in eight scrolls and a literary collection in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Explication of Common Sayings in eight juan and a collected works in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 杳字士深，年數歲，征士明僧紹見之，撫而言曰：「此兒實千里之駒。

translations.literal: Yao, style name Shishen, when several years old, the recluse Ming Sengshao saw him, stroked him, and said, "This child is truly a horse of a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao, styled Shishen, was still a small boy when the recluse Ming Sengshao met him, stroked his head, and said, "This boy is a steed that will cover a thousand leagues.

sentences.zh: 」十三丁父憂，每哭，哀感行路。

translations.literal: " At thirteen he entered mourning for his father; whenever he wept, grief moved those on the road.
translations.idiomatic: " At thirteen he mourned his father; each time he wept, passers-by were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 梁天監中，為宣惠豫章王行參軍。

translations.literal: In the Tianjian era of Liang he served as Acting Retainer to the Prince of Yuzhang, Heir of Xuanhui.
translations.idiomatic: During Liang Tianjian he served as acting retainer to Prince Xuanhui of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 杳博綜群書，沈約、任昉以下每有遺忘，皆訪問焉。

translations.literal: Yao comprehensively mastered the many books; Shen Yue, Ren Fang, and those below whenever they had something forgotten, all inquired of him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao commanded the breadth of the classics; whenever Shen Yue, Ren Fang, or their peers forgot a detail, they came to him.

sentences.zh: 嘗於約坐語及宗廟犧樽，約云：「鄭玄答張逸謂為畫鳳皇尾婆娑然。

translations.literal: Once at Yue's seat they spoke of the temple sacrificial goblet; Yue said, "Zheng Xuan, answering Zhang Yi, said it was painted with a phoenix tail swaying gracefully.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Shen Yue's company the talk turned to the temple sacrificial goblet; Shen Yue said, "Zheng Xuan told Zhang Yi that it was painted with a phoenix tail, swaying gracefully.

sentences.zh: 今無復此器，則不依古。

translations.literal: Now there is no longer this vessel, then one does not follow antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Since the vessel no longer exists, we need not follow the ancient form.

sentences.zh: 」杳曰：「此言未必可安。

translations.literal: " Yao said, "This statement is not necessarily secure.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Yao replied, "That reading is not necessarily sound.

sentences.zh: 古者樽彝皆刻木為鳥獸，鑿頂及背以出內酒。

translations.literal: In antiquity zun and yi vessels were all carved in wood into birds and beasts, with the crown and back bored to pour out the wine within.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity sacrificial goblets were carved as birds and beasts, with holes bored through crown and back so the wine could be poured out.

sentences.zh: 魏時魯郡地中得齊大夫子尾送女器，有犧樽作犧牛形。

translations.literal: In Wei times from the ground in Lu commandery was obtained the vessel in which the Qi grandee Ziwei sent off his daughter; among them was a sacrificial goblet made in the shape of a sacrificial ox.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei times excavators in Lu commandery found the dowry vessels of the Qi minister Ziwei, including a sacrificial goblet shaped like a sacrificial ox.

sentences.zh: 晉永嘉中，賊曹嶷于青州發齊景公塚又得二樽，形亦為牛象。

translations.literal: In Jin Yongjia, the bandit Cao Yi at Qingzhou excavated Duke Jing of Qi's tomb and again obtained two goblets, their shape also that of oxen.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Yongjia the rebel Cao Yi opened Duke Jing of Qi's tomb in Qingzhou and found two more goblets, likewise in the form of oxen.

sentences.zh: 二處皆古之遺器，知非虛也。

translations.literal: Both places yielded ancient surviving vessels; one knows it was not empty talk.
translations.idiomatic: Both finds were genuine antiquities, which shows the account was no fiction.

sentences.zh: 」約大以為然。

translations.literal: " Yue greatly considered it so.
translations.idiomatic: " Shen Yue was fully persuaded.

sentences.zh: 約又云：「何承天纂文奇博，其書載張仲師及長頸王事，此何所出？

translations.literal: Yue also said, "He Chengtian's compiled writings are marvelously broad; his book records Zhang Zhongshi and the Long-Necked King—where does this come from?
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue added, "He Chengtian's anthology is wonderfully vast, yet it cites Zhang Zhongshi and the Long-Necked King—what are his sources?

sentences.zh: 」杳曰：「仲師長尺二寸，唯出論衡。

translations.literal: " Yao said, "Zhongshi was one foot two inches tall; he appears only in Discourses Weighed.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Yao answered, "Zhongshi stood a foot and two inches tall and is mentioned only in Discourses Weighed.

sentences.zh: 長頸是毗騫王，朱建安扶南以南記云：'古來至今不死'。

translations.literal: The long neck is King Virudhaka; Zhu Jian'an's Record South of Funan from Fufan says, 'From antiquity to the present he does not die.'
translations.idiomatic: The long-necked figure is King Virudhaka; Zhu Jian'an's Record of Lands South of Funan says, 'From ancient times to now he has not died.'

sentences.zh: 」約即取二書尋檢，一如杳言。

translations.literal: " Yue immediately took the two books and searched; all was as Yao had said.
translations.idiomatic: " Shen Yue fetched both books at once and checked; everything matched Liu Yao's account.

sentences.zh: 約郊居宅時新構閣齋，杳為贊二首，並以所撰文章呈約，約即命工書人題其贊於壁。

translations.literal: When Yue's suburban residence had a newly built tower studio, Yao composed two encomia and also presented to Yue writings he had composed; Yue immediately ordered a scribe to inscribe the encomia on the wall.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Yue built a new pavilion at his country house, Liu Yao offered two encomia and his latest essays; Shen Yue had a clerk copy the encomia onto the walls.

sentences.zh: 仍報杳書，共相歎美。

translations.literal: He also replied to Yao in writing, and together they sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote back to Liu Yao, and the two men marveled at each other's work.

sentences.zh: 又在任昉坐，有人餉昉沖酒而作搌字，昉問杳此字是不，杳曰：「葛洪字苑作木旁右。

translations.literal: Again, at Ren Fang's seat, someone presented Fang with chong wine and wrote the character with the hand radical; Fang asked Yao whether this character was correct, and Yao said, "Ge Hong's Garden of Characters makes it wood at the side, you at the right."
translations.idiomatic: Once at Ren Fang's table a guest brought chong wine and wrote the name with the 'hand' radical; Ren Fang asked Liu Yao if the character was right, and Liu Yao said, "Ge Hong's Garden of Characters writes it with 'wood' beside 'you.'"

sentences.zh: 」昉又曰：「酒有千日醉，當是虛言。

translations.literal: Fang also said, "Wine that intoxicates for a thousand days must be empty talk."
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fang also said, "Wine that keeps one drunk for a thousand days must be a fable."

sentences.zh: 」杳曰：「桂陽程鄉有千里酒，飲之至家而醉。

translations.literal: Yao said, "In Guiyang's Cheng district there is thousand-li wine; drink it and one is drunk only upon reaching home.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao said, "In Cheng township of Guiyang there is 'thousand-league wine'; you drink it on the road and do not grow drunk until you reach home.

sentences.zh: 亦其例。

translations.literal: This too is of that kind.
translations.idiomatic: That is the same sort of thing.

sentences.zh: 」昉大驚曰：「吾自當遺忘，實不憶此。

translations.literal: Fang was greatly startled and said, "I myself must have forgotten; I truly do not recall this."
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fang was astonished and said, "I must have forgotten it myself; I truly have no memory of this."

sentences.zh: 」杳云：「出楊元鳳所撰置郡事。

translations.literal: Yao said, "It comes from Yang Yuanfeng's compiled Record of Established Commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao said, "It comes from Yang Yuanfeng's Record of Established Commanderies.

sentences.zh: 元鳳是魏代人，此書仍載其賦'三重五品，商溪況裏'。

translations.literal: Yuanfeng was a man of Wei; this book still preserves his rhapsody, 'Triple ranks and five grades, Shang Stream and Kuang Village.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfeng lived in Wei times, and the book still preserves his rhapsody: 'Triple ranks and five grades, Shang Stream and Kuang Village.'

sentences.zh: 」昉即檢楊記，言皆不差。

translations.literal: Fang immediately examined Yang's record; the words were without discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fang looked up Yang's record at once and found not a word amiss.

sentences.zh: 王僧孺被使撰譜，訪杳血脈所因。

translations.literal: Wang Sengru was commissioned to compile genealogies and inquired of Yao on what the bloodlines depended.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengru was ordered to compile genealogies and asked Liu Yao how the lineages should be traced.

sentences.zh: 杳云：「桓譚新論云：'太史三代世表旁行邪上，並效周譜。

translations.literal: Yao said, "Huan Tan's New Discourses says, 'The Grand Historian's Genealogical Tables of Three Dynasties run sideways and slant upward, all modeled on Zhou genealogies.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao said, "Huan Tan's New Discourses states, 'The Grand Historian's Genealogical Tables of the Three Dynasties run in lateral columns that slant upward, all imitating Zhou house genealogies.'

sentences.zh: '以此而推，當起周代。

translations.literal: By this one infers that it should begin in the Zhou era.
translations.idiomatic: From that one may infer that the practice began in Zhou times.

sentences.zh: 」僧孺歎曰：「可謂得所未聞。

translations.literal: Sengru sighed and said, "One may say you have obtained what was never heard before."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengru exclaimed, "That is truly something no one had heard before."

sentences.zh: 」周舍又問杳尚書著紫荷橐，相傳云挈囊，竟何所出？

translations.literal: Zhou She also asked Yao why Masters of Writing wear the purple lotus pouch, tradition saying 'grasping the pouch'—what is its ultimate origin?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou She also asked Liu Yao why Masters of Writing wear the purple lotus satchel, and why tradition speaks of 'grasping the pouch'—where does that come from?

sentences.zh: 「杳曰：「張安世傳云：'持橐簪筆，事孝武皇帝數十年。

translations.literal: Yao said, "Zhang Anshi's biography says, 'Holding the pouch and pinning the brush, serving Emperor Xiaowu of Han for several tens of years.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao said, "Zhang Anshi's biography reads, 'He held the pouch and pinned the brush, serving Emperor Wu of Han for decades.'

sentences.zh: '韋昭、張晏注並曰：'橐，囊也。

translations.literal: Wei Zhao's and Zhang Yan's commentaries both say, 'Pouch means satchel.'
translations.idiomatic: The commentaries of Wei Zhao and Zhang Yan both explain, 'Pouch means satchel.'

sentences.zh: 簪筆以待顧問。

translations.literal: Pinning the brush to await consultation.
translations.idiomatic: He pinned the brush to be ready when the emperor called for counsel.

sentences.zh: '範岫撰字書音訓又訪杳焉。

translations.literal: Fan Xiu, compiling his Character Book with phonetic glosses, also consulted Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xiu, compiling his dictionary of characters and readings, likewise sought Liu Yao's help.

sentences.zh: 尋佐周舍撰國史。

translations.literal: Soon after he assisted Zhou She in compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He soon assisted Zhou She in compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 出為臨津令，有善績，秩滿，縣三百餘人詣闕請留，敕許焉。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Linjin; he had good achievements, and when his term ended more than three hundred men of the district went to the gate to request that he remain; an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as magistrate of Linjin and governed well; when his term ended more than three hundred local men went to court to ask that he stay, and the throne granted their request.

sentences.zh: 後詹事徐勉舉杳及顧協等五人入華林撰遍略，書成，以晉安王府參軍兼廷尉正，以足疾解。

translations.literal: Later the Household Steward Xu Mian recommended Yao together with Gu Xie and four others to enter Hualin and compile the Comprehensive Digest; when the book was finished he became Retainer to the Prince of Jin'an and concurrently Rectifier in the Court of Judicial Review, but resigned because of foot ailment.
translations.idiomatic: Later Steward of the Heir Apparent Xu Mian nominated Liu Yao, Gu Xie, and three others to compile the Comprehensive Digest in Hualin Park; when the work was done he served as retainer to the Prince of Jin'an and concurrently as rectifier in the Court of Judicial Review, then resigned on account of foot trouble.

sentences.zh: 因著林庭賦，王僧孺見而歎曰：「郊居以後，無復此作。

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed "Rhapsody on the Forest Court"; Wang Sengru saw it and sighed, "After Dwelling in the Suburbs there has been no work like this again."
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote his Rhapsody on the Forest Court; Wang Sengru read it and sighed, "Since Shen Yue's Dwelling in the Suburbs, nothing has equaled this."

sentences.zh: 」累遷尚書儀曹郎，僕射徐勉以台閣文議專委杳焉。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Gentleman of Ceremonies in the Ministry of Rites; Vice Director Xu Mian entrusted to Yao alone the literary deliberations of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to gentleman of ceremonies in the Ministry of Rites; Vice Director Xu Mian entrusted all secretariat drafting to him alone.

sentences.zh: 出為余姚令，在縣清潔。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Yuyao; in the district he was pure and clean.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as magistrate of Yuyao and kept the district scrupulously clean.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹發教褒美之。

translations.literal: Prince Dong of Xiangdong Xiao Yi issued an instruction praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong issued an edict commending him.

sentences.zh: 大通元年，為步兵校尉，兼東宮通事舍人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong he became Commandant of Footsoldiers and concurrently Palace Attendant for Communications in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong he became commandant of footsoldiers and concurrently palace attendant for communications in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 昭明太子謂曰：「酒非卿所好，而為酒廚之職，政為卿不愧古人耳。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhaoming said to him, "Wine is not what you care for, yet you hold the post of the wine kitchen—precisely because you do not disgrace the ancients."
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhaoming told him, "You care little for wine, yet you hold charge of the palace wine stores—because even in that office you do not shame the ancients."

sentences.zh: 」太子有瓠食器，因以賜焉，曰：「卿有古人之風，故遺卿古人之器。

translations.literal: The crown prince had a gourd food vessel and therefore bestowed it on him, saying, "You have the air of the ancients; hence I leave you an ancient man's vessel."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince owned a gourd serving bowl and gave it to him, saying, "You carry the spirit of the ancients, so I leave you an ancient man's vessel."

sentences.zh: 」俄有敕代裴子野知著作郎事。

translations.literal: Soon an edict came that he should replace Pei Ziye in charge of the affairs of the Clerk of Writings.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict named him to replace Pei Ziye as clerk of writings.

sentences.zh: 昭明太子薨，新宮建，舊人例無停者，敕特留杳焉。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Zhaoming died and the new palace was built, by precedent the old staff were not retained, but an edict specially kept Yao.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Zhaoming died and a new heir was installed, former staff were normally dismissed, but Liu Yao was specially retained by edict.

sentences.zh: 僕射何敬容奏轉杳王府諮議，武帝曰：「劉杳須先經中書。

translations.literal: Vice Director He Jingrong memorialized to transfer Yao to Adviser of the Prince's Household, and Emperor Wu said, "Liu Yao must first pass through the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director He Jingrong proposed moving Liu Yao to adviser of the prince's household, but Emperor Wu said, "Liu Yao must first serve in the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 」仍除中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon made gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋為平西湘東諮議參軍，兼舍人、著作如故。

translations.literal: Soon he became Adviser to the Pacification-Western Army of Xiangdong and concurrently Attendant and Clerk of Writings as before.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became adviser to Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong's Pacification-Western headquarters, retaining his posts as attendant and clerk of writings.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左丞，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left vice director of the Ministry of State Affairs and died in office.

sentences.zh: 杳清儉無所嗜好，自居母憂，便長斷腥膻，持齋蔬食。

translations.literal: Yao was pure and frugal and without indulgences; from the time he dwelt in mourning for his mother he long cut off fish and meat and kept a vegetarian fast.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao lived plainly and without indulgence; from his mother's mourning onward he forever renounced meat and fish and ate only vegetarian fare.

sentences.zh: 臨終遺命：「斂以法服，載以露車，還葬舊墓，隨得一地，容棺而已。

translations.literal: At the end he left instructions: "Let the encoffinment use the dharma garments, carry on an open cart, return to burial in the old tomb; wherever one plot suffices, let it hold the coffin only.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he instructed his heirs: "Dress me in monastic robes, carry me on an open cart, and bury me in the family grave wherever a plot will hold the coffin.

sentences.zh: 不得設靈筵及祭醊。

translations.literal: Do not set up a spirit altar or sacrificial libations."
translations.idiomatic: Set up no mourning altar and offer no sacrificial feasts."

sentences.zh: 」其子遵行之。

translations.literal: His son carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: His son obeyed.

sentences.zh: 撰要雅五卷，楚辭草木疏一卷，高士傳二卷，東宮新舊記三十卷，古今四部書目五卷，文集十五卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: He compiled Essentials and Elegance in five scrolls, Commentary on the Plants and Trees of the Songs of Chu in one scroll, Biographies of Exalted Men in two scrolls, Old and New Records of the Eastern Palace in thirty scrolls, Catalogue of Books Ancient and Modern in Four Sections in five scrolls, and a literary collection in fifteen scrolls, all circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Essentials and Elegance in five juan, a commentary on the flora of the Songs of Chu in one juan, Biographies of Exalted Men in two juan, Old and New Records of the Eastern Palace in thirty juan, a catalogue of ancient and modern books in four divisions in five juan, and collected works in fifteen juan, all of which circulated.

sentences.zh: 歊字士光，生夕有香氣，氛氳滿室。

translations.literal: Xiao, style name Shiguang, at birth in the evening there was fragrance; mist and vapor filled the room.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiao, styled Shiguang, was born at dusk amid a fragrance that filled the room.

sentences.zh: 幼有識慧，四歲喪父，與群兒同處，獨不戲弄。

translations.literal: In youth he had understanding and wisdom; at four he lost his father, and among the group of children he alone did not play.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he showed uncommon intelligence; when his father died at four he would not join the other children at play.

sentences.zh: 六歲誦論語、毛詩，意所不解，便能問難。

translations.literal: At six he recited the Analects and Mao Odes; what his mind did not understand he could at once question and challenge.
translations.idiomatic: At six he could recite the Analects and the Mao Odes, and whatever puzzled him he would question until it yielded.

sentences.zh: 十二讀莊子逍遙篇曰：「此可解耳。

translations.literal: At twelve he read Zhuangzi's chapter "Free and Easy Wandering" and said, "This can be understood."
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he read Zhuangzi's "Free and Easy Wandering" and declared, "This is plain enough."

sentences.zh: 」客問之，隨問而答，皆有情理，家人每異之，謂為神童。

translations.literal: When guests questioned him, he answered as they asked; all had feeling and principle; the family each time marveled at him, calling him a divine child.
translations.idiomatic: Guests tested him with questions and he answered each to the point; his family marveled and called him a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 及長，博學有文才，不娶不仕，與族弟籲並隱居求志，遨遊林澤，以山水書籍相娛而已。

translations.literal: When grown he was broadly learned and had literary talent; he did not marry and did not take office, and with his cousin Yu he together dwelt in seclusion seeking their aim, roaming forests and marshes, taking only mountains, waters, books, and writings as their pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood, he was learned and gifted with words; he neither married nor served office, and with his cousin Liu Yu he withdrew to seek their own path, roaming forests and streams and finding joy only in landscape and books.

sentences.zh: 奉母兄以孝悌稱，寢食不離左右。

translations.literal: He served his mother and elder brother and was praised for filial piety and brotherly respect; in sleeping and eating he did not leave their sides.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for his mother and elder brother and was known for filial devotion; he scarcely left their side by day or night.

sentences.zh: 母意有所須，口未及言，歊已先知，手自營辦，狼狽供奉。

translations.literal: When his mother's mind had some need, before her mouth had reached speech Xiao already knew beforehand and with his own hands arranged it, flustered in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever his mother needed, she had only to think it before Liu Xiao had already prepared it, hurrying to serve her.

sentences.zh: 母每疾病，夢歊進藥，及翌日轉有間效，其誠感如此。

translations.literal: Whenever his mother fell ill, she dreamed Xiao presented medicine, and on the next day there would often be improvement; his sincerity moved things to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: When she fell ill she would dream that Liu Xiao brought her medicine, and the next day she often improved; such was the power of his devotion.

sentences.zh: 性重興樂，尤愛山水，登危履嶮，必盡幽遐，人莫能及，皆歎其有濟勝之具。

translations.literal: By nature he greatly delighted in scenery and music, especially loving mountains and waters; climbing peril and treading precipices, he always exhausted the remote and hidden; people could not keep up, and all sighed that he had the equipment to master lofty places.
translations.idiomatic: He loved landscape and music above all, especially mountains and streams; on dangerous heights he always pressed to the farthest view, leaving others behind, and all said he was born to climb.

sentences.zh: 常欲避人世，以母老不忍違。

translations.literal: He often wished to avoid the human world, but because his mother was old he could not bear to go against her.
translations.idiomatic: He longed to leave the world of men, but his mother's age kept him from going.

sentences.zh: 每隨兄霽、杳從宦。

translations.literal: He often followed his elder brothers Ji and Yao in their official posts.
translations.idiomatic: He often accompanied his brothers Ji and Yao when they took office.

sentences.zh: 少時好施，務周人之急，人或遺之，亦不拒也。

translations.literal: In youth he delighted in giving and strove to relieve others' urgencies; when people presented things to him he also did not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved to give and made a point of helping those in distress; he never refused gifts either.

sentences.zh: 久而歎曰：「受人者必報；

translations.literal: After a long while he sighed and said, "One who receives from others must repay;
translations.idiomatic: In time he sighed and said, "Whoever accepts a gift must repay it;

sentences.zh: 不則有愧於人。

translations.literal: otherwise there is shame toward others.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise he lives in debt to others.

sentences.zh: 吾固無以報人，豈可常有愧乎。

translations.literal: I fundamentally have nothing with which to repay others—how can I constantly harbor shame?"
translations.idiomatic: I have nothing with which to repay anyone—how can I go on accepting shame forever?"

sentences.zh: 」天監十七年，忽著革終論。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Tianjian he suddenly composed the Discourse on Revising the End.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year seventeen he suddenly wrote his Discourse on Revising the End.

sentences.zh: 以為：

translations.literal: He held that:
translations.idiomatic: In it he argued:

sentences.zh: 形者無知之質，神者有知之性。

translations.literal: The form is substance without knowing; the spirit is nature with knowing.
translations.idiomatic: The body is matter without awareness; the spirit is awareness itself.

sentences.zh: 有知不獨存，依無知以自立，故形之於神，逆旅之館耳。

translations.literal: Knowing does not exist alone; it relies on the unknowing to establish itself—hence the form toward the spirit is like an inn on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Awareness cannot stand alone but depends on insensate matter, so the body is to the spirit only a traveler's lodge.

sentences.zh: 及其死也，神去此館，速朽得理。

translations.literal: When it reaches death, the spirit leaves this inn; swift decay is the right principle.
translations.idiomatic: At death the spirit quits that lodge, and swift decay is only fitting.

sentences.zh: 是以子羽沈川，漢伯方壙，文楚黃壤，士安麻索：此四子者得理也。

translations.literal: Therefore Ziyu sank in the river, Han Bo used a square mound, Wen Chu had yellow earth, and Shi'an used hemp cord: these four men obtained the right principle.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Wang Ziyu drowned in the river, Han Bo was buried under a square mound, Wen Chu under yellow earth, and Shi'an in hempen bindings—these four grasped the truth.

sentences.zh: 若從四子而游，則平生之志得矣。

translations.literal: If one roamed with the four men, then the ambition of a lifetime would be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: To follow those four would fulfill a life's true aim.

sentences.zh: 然積習生常，難卒改革，一朝肆志，儻不見從。

translations.literal: Yet accumulated habit becomes the constant, and reform is hard to complete at once; if one day indulges one's will, perhaps one will not be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet habit hardens into custom and cannot be broken in a day; to act on impulse at once may win no followers.

sentences.zh: 今欲翦截煩厚，務存儉易，進不裸屍，退異常俗，不傷存者之念，有合至人之道。

translations.literal: Now I wish to cut away the burdensome and thick, striving to keep what is spare and easy: advancing, not to leave the corpse naked; retreating, to differ from ordinary custom—without injuring the thoughts of the living, and in accord with the way of the perfected man.
translations.idiomatic: I mean now to strip away excess and keep only what is spare: not to leave the corpse unclothed, yet to depart from vulgar display, so as not to burden the living and to accord with the sage's way.

sentences.zh: 且張奐止用幅巾，王肅唯盥手足，范冉斂畢便葬，爰珍無設筵几，文度故舟為棺，子廉牛車載柩，叔起誡絕墳隴，康成使無卜吉。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhang Huan used only a headcloth, Wang Su washed only hands and feet, Fan Ran was buried as soon as encoffinment was finished, Yuan Zhen set out no banqueting tables, Wen Du formerly used a boat as coffin, Zilian used an ox cart to carry the bier, Shuji warned against tombs and mounds, and Kangcheng ordered no divination for a lucky site.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huan was buried with only a headcloth, Wang Su with washing of hands and feet alone, Fan Ran was interred the moment the coffin was closed, Yuan Zhen allowed no feast, Wen Du once used a boat for a coffin, Zilian carried his father's bier in an ox cart, Shuji forbade tombs and mounds, and Zheng Xuan left no geomancy for a lucky plot.

sentences.zh: 此數公者，尚或如之，況為吾人，而尚華泰。

translations.literal: These several gentlemen still acted thus; how much more for men like us, yet still to prize splendor and ease.
translations.idiomatic: Even such men chose simplicity; how much more should we, who are no greater, cling to pomp?

sentences.zh: 今欲髣佛景行，以為軌則。

translations.literal: Now I wish to take their bright conduct as model and make it the rule.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore take their bright example as my rule.

sentences.zh: 氣絕不須復魂，盥漱而斂。

translations.literal: When breath is cut off, there is no need to recall the soul; wash and encoffin.
translations.idiomatic: When breath fails, do not call back the soul; wash the body and encoffin it.

sentences.zh: 以一千錢市成棺，單故裙衫，衣巾枕履。

translations.literal: Use a thousand cash to buy a plain coffin, a single old skirt and shirt, clothes, towel, pillow, and shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Buy a plain coffin for a thousand cash, with one old skirt and shirt, clothes, towel, pillow, and shoes.

sentences.zh: 此外送往之具，棺中常物，一不得有所施。

translations.literal: Beyond this, for things sent off, nothing whatsoever in the coffin may be placed.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these, nothing at all may go into the coffin for the journey.

sentences.zh: 世多信李、彭之言，可謂惑矣。

translations.literal: The age mostly believes the words of Li and Peng; one may call that delusion.
translations.idiomatic: The world mostly believes Laozi and Pengzu; that, I say, is delusion.

sentences.zh: 余以孔、釋為師，差無此惑。

translations.literal: I take Confucius and the Buddha as teachers; by comparison I have no such delusion.
translations.idiomatic: I take Confucius and the Buddha as my teachers and am free of that error.

sentences.zh: 斂訖，載以露車，歸於舊山，隨得一地，地足為坎，坎足容棺。

translations.literal: When encoffinment is finished, carry on an open cart and return to the old mountain; wherever one plot suffices, the ground enough for a pit, the pit enough to hold the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites of encoffinment are done, carry me on an open cart to the family hills; wherever the ground will hold a pit, and the pit a coffin, let that suffice.

sentences.zh: 不須磚甓，不勞封樹，勿設祭饗，勿置几筵。

translations.literal: There is no need for brick or tile, no labor for sealing trees; do not set out sacrificial offerings, do not place tables and mats.
translations.idiomatic: Use no brick facing, plant no grave trees, set out no sacrificial feast, and lay no mourning mats.

sentences.zh: 其蒸嘗繼嗣，言象所絕，事止餘身，無傷世教。

translations.literal: As for seasonal offerings and succession of heirs, the words and images are cut off; the affair stops with the body and does not harm worldly teaching.
translations.idiomatic: As for seasonal sacrifices and heirs to maintain them, I end such forms with my body and do no injury to public morals.

sentences.zh: 初，籲之疾，歊盡心救療，及卒哀傷，為之誄，又著悲友賦以序哀情。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yu fell ill, Xiao exhausted his mind to cure him; when he died Xiao mourned in grief, composed a eulogy for him, and also wrote "Rhapsody on Grieving for a Friend" to set forth the feeling of sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: When his cousin Liu Yu fell ill, Liu Xiao nursed him with all his strength; at Liu Yu's death he mourned deeply, wrote a eulogy, and composed his Rhapsody on Grieving for a Friend to record his grief.

sentences.zh: 忽有老人無因而至，謂曰：「君心力堅猛，必破死生；

translations.literal: Suddenly an old man came without cause and said to him, "Your mind's force is firm and fierce; you will surely break through birth and death;
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly an old man appeared from nowhere and said, "Your will is fierce and steadfast; you will surely pierce the barrier of life and death;

sentences.zh: 但運會所至，不得久留一方耳。

translations.literal: but the turn of fate that has arrived will not allow you to remain long in one place."
translations.idiomatic: but the turn your fate has taken will not let you linger long in one place."

sentences.zh: 」彈指而去。

translations.literal: He snapped his fingers and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He snapped his fingers and was gone.

sentences.zh: 歊心知其異，試遣尋之，莫知其所。

translations.literal: Xiao knew in his mind that this was strange and tried sending men to seek him, but none knew where he was.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiao knew the encounter was uncanny and sent men to find him, but no one could discover where he had gone.

sentences.zh: 於是信心彌篤。

translations.literal: Thereupon his faith grew ever more earnest.
translations.idiomatic: From that day his faith grew only firmer.

sentences.zh: 既而寢疾，恐貽母憂，乃自言笑，勉進湯藥。

translations.literal: Before long he took to his bed in illness; fearing he would leave distress to his mother, he himself spoke and laughed and forced himself to take broth and medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he fell ill; lest he grieve his mother, he made light of his pain, jested, and forced himself to take broth and medicine.

sentences.zh: 謂兄霽、杳曰：「兩兄祿仕，足伸供養。

translations.literal: He said to his brothers Ji and Yao: "Both elder brothers hold salaried office, enough to extend support."
translations.idiomatic: He told his brothers Liu Ji and Liu Yao, "You both hold salaried posts—enough to provide for our mother."

sentences.zh: 歊之歸泉，復何所憾。

translations.literal: Xiao's return to the springs—again, what regret remains?
translations.idiomatic: When I go down to the springs, what will I have left to regret?

sentences.zh: 願深割無益之悲。

translations.literal: I wish you deeply to cut off useless grief.
translations.idiomatic: Please put aside grief that can do no good.

sentences.zh: 」十八年，年三十二卒。

translations.literal: " In the eighteenth year, aged thirty-two, he died.
translations.idiomatic: " He died in the eighteenth year of Tianjian, at thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 始沙門釋寶志遇歊於興皇寺，驚起曰：「隱居學道，清淨登仙。

translations.literal: Earlier the monk Shibao of the Buddhist order encountered Xiao at Xinghuang Temple, started up in alarm, and said: "Withdrawing to study the Way, in purity you will ascend as an immortal."
translations.idiomatic: Long before, the monk Baozhi met Liu Xiao at Xinghuang Temple, rose startled, and said, "You withdraw to cultivate the Way; in purity you will rise as an immortal."

sentences.zh: 」如此三說。

translations.literal: Thus he spoke three times.
translations.idiomatic: He said as much three times.

sentences.zh: 歊未死之春，有人為其庭中栽柿，歊謂兄子弇曰：「吾不見此實，爾其勿言。

translations.literal: In the spring before Xiao died, someone planted a persimmon in his courtyard; Xiao told his brother's son Yan: "I shall not see this fruit—do not speak of it."
translations.idiomatic: The spring before Liu Xiao died, someone planted a persimmon in his courtyard. He told his nephew Yan, "I will never see this fruit ripen—say nothing of it."

sentences.zh: 」至秋而亡，人以為知命。

translations.literal: " When autumn came he died, and people took it as knowledge of fate.
translations.idiomatic: " He died that autumn, and people called it foreknowledge of his end.

sentences.zh: 親故誄其行跡，諡曰貞節處士。

translations.literal: Relatives and friends composed a eulogy for his conduct and gave the posthumous title Recluse of Chastened Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen and friends wrote his elegy and gave him the posthumous name Chastity Recluse.

sentences.zh: 先是有太中大夫琅邪王敬胤以天監八年卒，遺命：「不得設復魄旌旐，一蘆笰藉下，一枚覆上。

translations.literal: Earlier there was Grand Master for Court Discussion Wang Jingyin of Langya, who died in the eighth year of Tianjian; his testament ran: "Do not set out the soul-recalling banners and pennants; one reed mat beneath and one cover above."
translations.idiomatic: Some time before, Wang Jingyin of Langya, Grand Master for Court Discussion, had died in Tianjian 8, leaving word: "Set up no soul-recalling banners or pennants—only one reed mat beneath and a single cover above."

sentences.zh: 吾氣絕便沐浴，籃輿載屍，還忠侯大夫隧中。

translations.literal: When my breath stops, bathe me at once; carry the corpse in a bamboo litter and return it to the tomb of the Loyal Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Bathe me as soon as I cease to breathe, carry my body in a wicker litter, and return me to the Loyal Marquis's tomb."

sentences.zh: 若不行此，則戮吾屍於九泉。

translations.literal: If this is not done, then hack my corpse in the Nine Springs.
translations.idiomatic: If you will not do this, hack my corpse apart in the underworld."

sentences.zh: 」敬胤外甥許慧詔因阮研以聞。

translations.literal: Jingyin's maternal nephew Xu Huizhao reported it through Ruan Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyin's nephew Xu Huizhao brought the matter to court through Ruan Yan.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「敬胤令其息崇素，氣絕便沐浴，藉以二蘆笰，鑿地周身，歸葬忠侯。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Jingyin ordered his son Chongsu that when breath ceases he is to be bathed at once, laid on two reed mats, the ground cut away all around the body, and buried at the Loyal Marquis's tomb."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Jingyin told his son Chongsu to bathe him at death, lay him between two reed mats, hollow the earth around the coffin, and bury him with the Loyal Marquis."

sentences.zh: 此達生之格言，賢夫玉匣石槨遠矣。

translations.literal: This is the maxim of one who comprehends life; how far he stands from jade cases and stone outer coffins!
translations.idiomatic: That is the wisdom of one who truly understands life—how far it is from jade cases and stone sarcophagi."

sentences.zh: 然子于父命，亦有所從有所不從。

translations.literal: Yet between son and father's command there are things a son may follow and things he may not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a son owes his father's command both obedience and discernment."

sentences.zh: 今崇素若信遺意，土周淺薄，屬辟不施，一朝見侵狐鼠，戮屍已甚。

translations.literal: If Chongsu now trusts the testament completely, with thin earth wrapped round the coffin and no tainted shroud applied, the moment foxes and rats molest him, to hack the corpse would be too harsh.
translations.idiomatic: If Chongsu follows the will to the letter—shallow earth, no protective dressing—foxes and rats may assault the body the very next day, and dismembering the corpse would be too cruel."

sentences.zh: 父可以訓子，子亦不可行之。

translations.literal: A father may admonish his son, but a son need not carry every command out.
translations.idiomatic: A father may instruct his son, but a son is not bound to do all he is told."

sentences.zh: 外內易棺，此自奉親之情，藉土而葬，亦通人之意。

translations.literal: Exchanging inner and outer coffins accords with the feeling of serving one's parent; burial with earth also meets the common person's intent.
translations.idiomatic: A proper outer coffin honors parental feeling; burial in earth accords with ordinary custom."

sentences.zh: 宜兩舍兩取，以達父子之志。

translations.literal: It is fitting to give up a little on each side and take a little from each, so as to fulfill both father and son's aims.
translations.idiomatic: The right course is to compromise on both sides so father and son alike may be satisfied."

sentences.zh: 棺周于身，土周於槨，去其牲奠，斂以時服。

translations.literal: Let the coffin enclose the body and earth enclose the coffin; remove the sacrificial victims, and encoffin him in the garments of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Let the coffin surround the body and earth surround the coffin; omit sacrificial animals and dress him in contemporary clothes."

sentences.zh: 一可以申情，二可以稱家。

translations.literal: First, feeling may be expressed; second, the household may be honored.
translations.idiomatic: Thus feeling is shown, and the household is not shamed."

sentences.zh: 禮教無違，生死無辱，此故當為安也。」

translations.literal: Ritual teaching is not violated, and in life and death there is no disgrace—this, therefore, should settle the matter."
translations.idiomatic: Rites are kept, and neither the living nor the dead are shamed—let this stand as the decision."

sentences.zh: 籲字彥度，懷珍從孫也。

translations.literal: Yu, style name Yandu, was a great-nephew of Huaiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, styled Yandu, was the grandson of Huaiwei's brother.

sentences.zh: 祖承宗，宋太宰參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chengzong was a staff officer in the Song Grand Commandant's office.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Liu Chengzong served as an aide in the Song Grand Commandant's office.

sentences.zh: 父靈真，齊鎮西諮議、武昌太守。

translations.literal: His father Lingzhen was adviser of the Pacifying West headquarters in Qi and Administrator of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Lingzhen was consultant to the Pacifying West headquarters and Administrator of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 籲幼稱純孝，數歲父母繼卒，吁居喪哭泣孺慕，幾至滅性，赴吊者莫不傷焉。

translations.literal: Yu in youth was famed for pure filiality; before he was many years old his parents died in succession; Yu in mourning wept with the devotion of a child, nearly ruining his life-force; those who came to offer condolences none failed to grieve.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Liu Yu was famed for filial devotion; his parents died in close succession while he was still young. He mourned with a child's inconsolable grief, nearly destroying himself, and every mourner who came was moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 後為伯父所養，事伯母及昆姊孝友篤至，為宗族所稱。

translations.literal: Later he was raised by his paternal uncle; in serving his aunt and elder and younger sisters he was filial and brotherly to the utmost, and the clan praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Raised thereafter by his uncle, he was unfailingly filial to his aunt and devoted to his sisters, and the whole clan spoke of him with praise.

sentences.zh: 自傷早孤，人有誤觸其諱者，未嘗不感結流涕。

translations.literal: Grieving that he had been orphaned early, whenever anyone unwittingly touched on the taboo names of his parents he never failed to be stricken and burst into tears.
translations.idiomatic: Still wounded by early orphanhood, he would weep whenever anyone unwittingly spoke his parents' names.

sentences.zh: 長兄絜為娉妻，克日成婚，籲聞而逃匿，事息乃還。

translations.literal: When his eldest brother Jie betrothed a wife and the day of marriage was fixed, Yu heard of it and fled into hiding, returning only when the affair had passed.
translations.idiomatic: When his eldest brother Jie set a wedding day, Liu Yu vanished until the ceremony had passed.

sentences.zh: 本州刺史張稷辟為主簿，主者檄召籲，乃掛檄於樹而逃。

translations.literal: The provincial governor Zhang Ji summoned him as chief clerk; the steward issued a summons for Yu, but he hung the notice on a tree and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji, governor of the province, appointed him chief clerk; when the summons arrived Liu Yu hung it on a tree and ran.

sentences.zh: 陳留阮孝緒博學隱居，不交當世，恒居一鹿床，環植竹木，寢處其中，時人造之，未嘗見也。

translations.literal: Ruan Xiaoxu of Chenliu was erudite and lived in seclusion, associating with no one of the age; he constantly dwelt on a single deer-bed, planting bamboo and trees all around, sleeping among them; when people of the time went to see him, he had never once received them.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Xiaoxu of Chenliu was learned and reclusive, keeping company with no one in public life. He lived on a deerwood couch amid a ring of bamboo and trees and would receive no caller.

sentences.zh: 籲經一造，孝緒即顧以神交。

translations.literal: Yu paid one visit, and Xiaoxu at once turned to him in spiritual friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu visited once, and Xiaoxu immediately embraced him as a kindred spirit.

sentences.zh: 籲族兄歊又履高操，三人日夕招攜，故都下謂之三隱。

translations.literal: Yu's clansman Xiao also upheld lofty conduct; the three daily summoned one another, and therefore the capital called them the Three Recluses.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Liu Xiao was equally withdrawn; the three spent their days together, and the capital dubbed them the Three Recluses.

sentences.zh: 籲善玄言，尤精意釋典，曾與歊聽講鍾山諸寺，因共卜築宋熙寺東澗，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Yu was skilled in Dark Learning and especially devoted himself to Buddhist scriptures; once he and Xiao listened to lectures in the Zhongshan monasteries and together chose a site east of Songxi Temple's stream to build, with the wish to end their days there.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu delighted in Dark Learning and the Buddhist canon; with Liu Xiao he heard lectures at the Zhongshan monasteries and chose a hillside east of Songxi Temple to build, intending to end their days there.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎何炯嘗遇之于路，曰：「此人風神穎俊，蓋荀奉倩、衛叔寶之流也。

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman of the Masters of Writing He Jiong once met him on the road and said: "This man's spirit and bearing are sharp and elevated—he is of the sort of Xun Fengqian and Wei Shuobao."
translations.idiomatic: He Jiong of the Secretariat met him on the road and said, "That man's bearing is brilliant—in the line of Xun Fengqian and Wei Shuobao."

sentences.zh: 」命駕造門，拒而不見。

translations.literal: " He ordered his carriage to his gate, but Yu declined and would not see him.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent his carriage to Liu Yu's door, but Liu Yu refused to receive him.

sentences.zh: 族祖孝標與書稱之曰：「籲超超越俗，如半天朱霞。

translations.literal: His collateral ancestor Xiaobiao wrote praising him: "Yu transcends the vulgar like cinnabar clouds at midday.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Liu Xiaobiao wrote, "Liu Yu rises above the common world like vermilion clouds at noon.

sentences.zh: 歊矯矯出塵，如云中白鶴。

translations.literal: Xiao towers above the dust like a white crane amid clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiao lifts free of the dust like a white crane in the clouds.

sentences.zh: 皆儉歲之粱稷，寒年之纖纊。」

translations.literal: Both are millet and grain for a lean year, fine cloth for a cold year."
translations.idiomatic: Both are grain in a famine year and warm cloth in a bitter winter."

sentences.zh: 籲嘗著谷皮巾，披納衣，每遊山澤，輒留連忘返。

translations.literal: Yu once wore a grain-bark cap and draped a cotton monk's robe; whenever he roamed mountains and marshes he lingered without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: He often wore a bark-cloth cap and cotton monastic robe, wandering mountains and streams until he forgot to return.

sentences.zh: 神理閑正，姿貌甚華，在林穀之間，意氣彌遠，或有遇之者，皆謂神人。

translations.literal: His spirit and bearing were serene and correct, his appearance very splendid; among forest and valley he seemed ever more distant in spirit; those who met him all called him a divine man.
translations.idiomatic: Serene in spirit and striking in looks, he seemed to grow more distant among the hills; those who chanced upon him took him for an immortal.

sentences.zh: 家甚貧苦，並日而食，隆冬之月，或無氈絮，籲處之晏然，人不覺其饑寒也。

translations.literal: His household was very poor and bitter; they ate alternate days; in the deep of winter sometimes there was no felt or cotton wadding, yet Yu dwelt in it calmly, and people did not perceive his hunger or cold.
translations.idiomatic: The household was desperately poor, eating only every other day; in deep winter they sometimes lacked quilted bedding, yet Liu Yu was unperturbed, and visitors never noticed his hunger or cold.

sentences.zh: 自少至長，無喜慍之色。

translations.literal: From youth to age he showed no color of joy or anger.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood to old age his face never showed joy or anger.

sentences.zh: 每於可競之地，輒以不競勝之。

translations.literal: In every place where one could compete, he prevailed by not competing.
translations.idiomatic: Where others strove for advantage, he won by refusing to strive.

sentences.zh: 或有加陵之者，莫不退而愧服，由是眾論咸歸重焉。

translations.literal: Some who insulted or overbore him all drew back ashamed and subdued; from this public opinion everywhere deferred to him.
translations.idiomatic: Those who bullied him withdrew abashed; by this the crowd everywhere came to honor him.

sentences.zh: 天監十七年，卒於歊舍。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Tianjian he died in Xiao's lodging.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Tianjian 17 at Liu Xiao's house.

sentences.zh: 臨終執歊手曰：「氣絕便斂，斂畢即埋，靈筵一不須立。

translations.literal: At the end he took Xiao's hand and said: "When breath ceases, encoffin at once; when encoffinment is finished, bury immediately; do not set up a mourning altar in the least."
translations.idiomatic: Dying, he clasped Liu Xiao's hand and said, "Encoffin me as soon as I stop breathing; bury me when that is done; erect no mourning altar."

sentences.zh: 勿設饗祀，無求繼嗣。

translations.literal: Do not set out feast-offerings; do not seek heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Offer no sacrificial feasts and find no successors."

sentences.zh: 」歊從而行之。

translations.literal: " Xiao followed and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Xiao obeyed.

sentences.zh: 宗人至友，相與刊石立銘，諡曰玄貞處士。

translations.literal: Kinsmen and close friends together carved stone and set up an inscription; his posthumous title was Recluse of Mysterious Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen and friends raised a stone inscription; his posthumous name was Mystic Integrity Recluse.

sentences.zh: 善明，懷珍族弟也。

translations.literal: Shanming was a clansman younger brother of Huaiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shanming was Huaiwei's clansman and junior.

sentences.zh: 父懷人，仕宋為齊、北海二郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Huairen served the Song as Administrator of Qi and Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Huairen had served the Song as Administrator of Qi and Beihai.

sentences.zh: 元嘉末，青州饑荒，人相食。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia, Qingzhou suffered famine; men ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yuanjia Qingzhou starved until men ate one another.

sentences.zh: 善明家有積粟，躬食饘粥，開倉以救，鄉里多獲全濟，百姓呼其家田為續命田。

translations.literal: Shanming's household had stored grain; he personally ate thin gruel, opened the storehouse to save others, and many in the village escaped with their lives; the common people called his family fields the Life-Continuation Fields.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanming household hoarded grain yet ate only thin porridge, opening the storehouse to aid neighbors. Many in the district were saved, and people called his family's fields the Fields of Restored Life.

sentences.zh: 善明少而靜處讀書，刺史杜驥聞名候之，辭不相見。

translations.literal: Shanming in youth quietly dwelt reading books; Governor Du Ji heard his name and called on him, but he declined and would not meet.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he read in quiet seclusion; when Governor Du Ji came to visit on account of his reputation, he refused to receive him.

sentences.zh: 年四十，刺史劉道隆辟為中從事。

translations.literal: At forty years the governor Liu Daolong summoned him as middle aide-de-camp.
translations.idiomatic: At forty Liu Daolong as governor appointed him middle aide-de-camp.

sentences.zh: 懷人謂善明曰：「我已知汝立身，復欲見汝立官也。

translations.literal: Huairen said to Shanming: "I already know how you will stand as a man; I wish next to see how you will stand in office."
translations.idiomatic: Huairen told him, "I know how you carry yourself as a man; now I wish to see how you carry yourself as an official."

sentences.zh: 」善明應辟，仍舉秀才。

translations.literal: " Shanming accepted the summons and was also nominated as Presented Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Shanming accepted the post and was nominated Presented Scholar.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武見其策強直，甚異之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Song saw his examination answers forceful and direct and marveled greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of Song read his examination papers—bold and unyielding—and was struck with wonder.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，徐州刺史薛安都反，青州刺史沈文秀應之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi, the Inspector of Xuzhou Xue An'du rebelled, and the Inspector of Qingzhou Shen Wenxiu answered him.
translations.idiomatic: In the opening of Taishi, Xue Andu as Inspector of Xuzhou rebelled, and Shen Wenxiu as Inspector of Qingzhou joined him.

sentences.zh: 時州居東陽城，善明家在郭內，不能自拔。

translations.literal: At the time the province was in Dongyang city; Shanming's family was inside the outer wall and could not break free.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial seat lay in Dongyang city; Liu Shanming's home was inside the walls and could not escape.

sentences.zh: 伯父彌之詭說文秀求自效，文秀使領軍主張靈慶等五千人援安都。

translations.literal: His uncle Mizhi with specious words persuaded Wenxiu to seek to offer his own service; Wenxiu sent the army commander Zhang Lingqing and others with five thousand men to aid An'du.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Mizhi won Wenxiu's trust with cunning words and was sent to lead five thousand men under Zhang Lingqing to reinforce Andu.

sentences.zh: 彌之出門，密謂部曲曰：「始免禍坑矣。

translations.literal: Mizhi left the gate and secretly told his troops: "At last we escape the pit of calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the city Mizhi whispered to his men, "At last we are out of the pit."

sentences.zh: 」行至下邳，乃背文秀，善明從伯懷恭為北海太守，據郡相應。

translations.literal: " When they reached Xiapi he turned against Wenxiu; Shanming's father's elder brother's brother Huaigong was Administrator of Beihai and held the commandery in answer to the court.
translations.idiomatic: " At Xiapi he betrayed Wenxiu; his cousin Huaigong as Administrator of Beihai held the prefecture for the throne.

sentences.zh: 善明密契，收集門宗部曲，得三千人。

translations.literal: Shanming by secret pledge gathered the clansmen and household retainers to three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: By secret compact Liu Shanming rallied kinsmen and retainers to three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 夜斬關奔北海。

translations.literal: At night he cut through the gate and fled to Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: By night he broke through the gate and fled to Beihai.

sentences.zh: 族兄乘人又聚眾勃海以應朝廷。

translations.literal: His clansman Chenren also gathered a host in Bohai to answer the court.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Chenren likewise raised troops in Bohai for the court.

sentences.zh: 而彌之尋為薛安都所殺，明帝贈青州刺史。

translations.literal: Mizhi before long was killed by Xue An'du, and Emperor Ming gave him posthumous appointment as Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mizhi was soon killed by Xue Andu; Emperor Ming posthumously named him Inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以乘人為冀州刺史，善明為北海太守，除尚書金部郎。

translations.literal: Chenren was made Inspector of Jizhou, Shanming Administrator of Beihai, and removed to Gentleman in the Ministry of Revenue's Gold Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Chenren was made Inspector of Jizhou; Liu Shanming became Administrator of Beihai and was promoted to Gentleman in the Gold Bureau of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 乘人病卒，仍以善明為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Chenren died of illness, and Shanming was again made Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenren died of illness Liu Shanming succeeded him as Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 文秀既降，除善明海陵太守，郡境邊海，無樹木，善明課人種榆檟雜果，遂獲其利。

translations.literal: When Wenxiu had surrendered, Shanming was appointed Administrator of Hailing; the commandery bordered the sea and had no trees; Shanming required people to plant elms, catalpa, and mixed fruit and thereby obtained the profit.
translations.idiomatic: After Wenxiu surrendered he was named Administrator of Hailing. The coast had no timber; Liu Shanming ordered the planting of elms, catalpa, and orchard trees until the district prospered.

sentences.zh: 還為直合將軍。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as General of the Straight Suite.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as General of the Straight Suite.

sentences.zh: 五年，魏克青州，善明母在焉，移置代郡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Wei took Qingzhou; Shanming's mother was there and was moved and settled in Dai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Northern Wei seized Qingzhou; his mother was taken and resettled in Dai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 善明布衣蔬食，哀戚如持喪，明帝每見，為之歎息。

translations.literal: Shanming wore cloth garments and ate simple food, grieving like one in mourning; whenever Emperor Ming saw him he sighed for him.
translations.idiomatic: He wore plain cloth and ate sparely, grieving as in mourning; Emperor Ming sighed whenever he saw him.

sentences.zh: 轉巴西梓潼二郡太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Administrator of Baxi and Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to dual Administrator of Baxi and Zitong.

sentences.zh: 善明以母在魏，不願西行，泣涕固請，見許。

translations.literal: Shanming, because his mother was in Wei, was unwilling to go west and wept, begging firmly; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His mother being in Wei territory, he wept and steadfastly refused to go west; the court allowed it.

sentences.zh: 朝廷多哀善明心事，元徽初遣北使，朝議令善明舉人。

translations.literal: The court much pitied Shanming's sentiments; at the beginning of Yuanhui envoys were sent north, and the court deliberation ordered Shanming to nominate someone.
translations.idiomatic: The court pitied his plight; when northern envoys were first sent in Yuanhui, Liu Shanming was asked to nominate one.

sentences.zh: 善明舉州鄉北平田惠紹使魏，贖母還。

translations.literal: Shanming nominated Tian Huishao of Beiping in his district and sent him to Wei to ransom his mother back.
translations.idiomatic: He nominated Tian Huishao of Beiping in his home district to go to Wei and ransom his mother home.

sentences.zh: 時宋後廢帝新立，群臣執政，善明獨事齊高帝，委身歸誠。

translations.literal: At the time the deposed Later Emperor of Song had newly taken the throne; the ministers held power; Shanming alone served Emperor Gao of Qi, giving himself in loyal devotion.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Deposed Emperor had just ascended, ministers ruled; Liu Shanming alone pledged himself to the future Emperor Gao of Qi.

sentences.zh: 出為西海太守，行青冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Xihai and acted as Inspector of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Administrator of Xihai and acted as Inspector of Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 善明從弟僧副與善明俱知名於鄉里，泰始初，魏攻淮北，僧副將部曲二千人東依海島。

translations.literal: Shanming's younger cousin Sengfu and Shanming were alike famed in their home district; at the beginning of Taishi, when Wei attacked north of the Huai, Sengfu led two thousand retainers east to rely on sea islands.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Sengfu was equally renowned at home; when Wei struck north of the Huai in Taishi's opening, Sengfu took two thousand retainers to refuge on coastal islands.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝在淮陰，壯其所為，召與相見，引為安成王撫軍參軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao of Qi was at Huaiyin, admired his conduct, summoned him to meet, and brought him in as staff officer to the Prince of Ancheng's Pacification Army.
translations.idiomatic: The future Emperor Gao at Huaiyin admired him, summoned him, and appointed him to the Pacification Army staff of the Prince of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝肆暴，高帝憂恐，常令僧副微行，伺察聲論。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor was wildly cruel; the High Emperor was anxious and fearful, and constantly had Sengfu travel in disguise to spy on public talk.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor ruled with savage cruelty; Gao Di in anxiety sent Sengfu incognito to probe public sentiment.

sentences.zh: 使密告善明及東海太守垣崇祖，使動魏兵。

translations.literal: He had him secretly inform Shanming and the Administrator of Donghai Yuan Chongzu to stir Wei to move troops.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly told Liu Shanming and Donghai Administrator Yuan Chongzu to provoke northern military action.

sentences.zh: 善明勸靜以待之，高帝納焉。

translations.literal: Shanming urged waiting calmly; the High Emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shanming counseled patience; Gao Di agreed.

sentences.zh: 廢帝見殺，善明為高帝驃騎諮議、南東海太守，行南徐州事。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor was killed, Shanming became adviser to the Flying Cavalry general-in-chief for Gao Di, Administrator of Southern Donghai, and acted in Southern Xuzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the Deposed Emperor's assassination Liu Shanming became adviser on Gao Di's staff, Administrator of Southern Donghai, and acting inspector of Southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之反，高帝深以為憂。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi rebelled, and the High Emperor was deeply worried.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi rebelled, and Gao Di was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 善明獻計曰：「沈攸之控引八州，縱情蓄斂，苞藏賊志，於焉十年。

translations.literal: Shanming presented a plan saying: "Shen Youzhi holds eight provinces, indulges his will in hoarding and levying, harbors rebel intent—thus for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shanming advised, "Shen Youzhi has held eight provinces for ten years, levying at will while nursing rebellion.

sentences.zh: 性既險躁，才非持重，起逆累旬，遲回不進，豈應有所待也？

translations.literal: By nature he is dangerous and rash, and his talent is not steady; he has raised rebellion for successive weeks yet delays and does not advance—could he be waiting for something?
translations.idiomatic: He is rash by nature and lacks steadiness; weeks into revolt he still hangs back—what can he be waiting for?

sentences.zh: 一則闇於兵機，二則人情離怨，三則有掣肘之患，四則天奪其魄。

translations.literal: First he is dark to military opportunity; second, men's hearts are alienated and resentful; third, there is the affliction of having one's arms checked; fourth, Heaven has taken his soul.
translations.idiomatic: First, he does not understand the art of war; second, his men are estranged and resentful; third, he suffers from divided command; fourth, Heaven has stolen his wits.

sentences.zh: 本疑其輕速，掩襲未備；

translations.literal: I had suspected his lightness and speed, that he would strike before we were ready;
translations.idiomatic: I had feared he would move swiftly and strike before we were prepared;

sentences.zh: 今六師齊奮，諸侯同舉，此已籠之鳥耳。

translations.literal: now the six armies rise together and the feudal lords act as one—he is already a bird in the cage.
translations.idiomatic: but now the imperial hosts rise as one and the lords all answer—he is a bird already caged.

sentences.zh: 」事平，高帝召善明還都，謂曰：「卿策沈攸之，雖張良、陳平適如此耳。

translations.literal: " When the affair was settled the High Emperor summoned Shanming back to the capital and said: "Your plotting against Shen Youzhi—even Zhang Liang and Chen Ping could do no more than this."
translations.idiomatic: " When the revolt ended Gao Di recalled him and said, "Your reading of Shen Youzhi would do credit to Zhang Liang or Chen Ping.

sentences.zh: 」仍遷太尉右司馬。

translations.literal: " He was then promoted to Right Marshal of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to Right Marshal of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 齊台建，為右衛將軍，辭疾不拜。

translations.literal: When the Qi regime was established he was made Right Guard General but declined on grounds of illness and did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was founded he was made Right Guard General but declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 司空褚彥回謂善明曰：「高尚之事，乃卿從來素意，今朝廷方相委待，詎得便學松、喬邪。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Chu Yanhui said to Shanming: "The matter of lofty retirement has always been your constant wish; now the court is about to entrust you in turn—how can you at once imitate Song and Qiao?"
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Chu Yanhuai told him, "Withdrawal to lofty retirement has always been your bent—surely you cannot now play the hermit like the immortals of Mount Song?"

sentences.zh: 」善明答曰：「我本無宦情，既逢知己，所以戮力驅馳。

translations.literal: Shanming replied: "I originally had no desire for office; having met a knowing lord, I therefore exerted my strength in the chariot traces.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shanming answered, "I never sought office; meeting a lord who knew my worth, I threw myself into his service.

sentences.zh: 天地廓清，朝廷濟濟，鄙吝既申，不敢昧于富貴矣。」

translations.literal: Heaven and earth are broad and cleared, the court is full and ordered; my narrow parsimony has had its day, and I dare not be blind to riches and honor."
translations.idiomatic: Now heaven and earth are clear and the court in good order; I have done my humble part and dare not shut my eyes to rank and reward."

sentences.zh: 高帝踐阼，以善明勳誠，欲與之祿，召謂曰：「淮南近畿，國之形勝，非親賢不居，卿與我臥理之。
