translations.literal: When the High Emperor took the throne, because of Shanming's meritorious loyalty he wished to grant him salary and summoned him, saying: "Huainan is near the capital, the state's strategic terrain; none but an intimate worthy may hold it—govern it with me from repose."
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Di ascended the throne he wished to reward Liu Shanming's loyalty, summoned him, and said, "Huainan borders the capital—it is the realm's key ground. Only a trusted worthy may hold it; govern it with me from your couch."

sentences.zh: 」乃代明帝為淮南宣城二郡太守。

translations.literal: " He was then appointed in Emperor Ming's stead governor of the two commanderies Huainan and Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Di then named him governor of Huainan and Xuancheng, replacing the Song Ming court's hold on those posts.

sentences.zh: 遣使拜授，封新淦伯。

translations.literal: Messengers were sent to invest him with the appointment, and he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingan.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were dispatched to confer the post, and he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingan.

sentences.zh: 善明至郡，上表陳事凡一十一條：其一以為「天地開創，宜存問遠方，廣宣慈澤」。

translations.literal: When Shanming reached the commandery he submitted a memorial setting forth eleven items in all. The first held that "Heaven and Earth are newly opened; one ought to inquire after distant regions and broadly proclaim merciful grace."
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post Liu Shanming memorialized the throne with eleven proposals. The first urged that, with the realm newly founded, the court should reach out to distant lands and spread benevolent rule far and wide.

sentences.zh: 其二以為「京都遠近所歸，宜遣醫藥，問其疾苦，年九十以上及六疾不能自存者，隨宜量賜」。

translations.literal: The second held that "The capital is what near and far look to; one ought to send physicians and medicine and inquire into their hardships and illness; those ninety years of age and above and those with the six afflictions who cannot support themselves ought to receive suitable grants as appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: The second urged that the capital draws the eyes of the empire, and that the court should send doctors and medicines, inquire into the people's ills, and grant relief as needed to anyone ninety or older or stricken with disability who could not survive without aid.

sentences.zh: 其三以為「宋氏赦令，蒙原者寡。

translations.literal: The third held that "Under the Song house's amnesty edicts, few have received pardon and restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The third noted that under the Song dynasty's repeated amnesties, few offenders had actually been pardoned or restored to their rights.

sentences.zh: 愚謂今下赦書，宜令事實相副」。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that the amnesty now to be issued ought to make deed and word match."
translations.idiomatic: He argued that the next amnesty should make promise and practice truly align."

sentences.zh: 其四以為「劉昶猶存，容能送死境上，諸城宜應嚴備」。

translations.literal: The fourth held that "Liu Chang still lives and may yet bring deadly trouble to the frontier; the border cities ought accordingly to be strictly guarded."
translations.idiomatic: The fourth warned that Liu Chang was still alive and might yet stir a fatal clash on the border, and that frontier garrisons should stand on full alert.

sentences.zh: 其五以為「宜除宋氏大明以來苛政細制，以崇簡易」。

translations.literal: The fifth held that "One ought to abolish the harsh policies and minute regulations since the Song Dayuan era, to honor simplicity and ease."
translations.idiomatic: The fifth called for scrapping the harsh laws and petty rules imposed since Emperor Ming of Song's Dayuan reign, in favor of plain and simple government.

sentences.zh: 其六以為「凡諸土木之費，且可權停」。

translations.literal: The sixth held that "All expenses for earthworks and timber construction may for the present be suspended by provisional order."
translations.idiomatic: The sixth asked that all public works and building costs be halted for the time being.

sentences.zh: 其七以為「帝子王女，宜崇儉約」。

translations.literal: The seventh held that "The emperor's sons and the royal princesses ought to be urged toward frugality and restraint."
translations.idiomatic: The seventh urged frugal living upon the imperial princes and princesses.

sentences.zh: 其八以為「宜詔百官及府州郡縣，各貢讜言，以弘廣唐、虞之美」。

translations.literal: The eighth held that "One ought to decree to the hundred officials and to the prefectures, provinces, commanderies, and counties that each present candid counsel, to extend and magnify the beauty of the eras of Tang and Yu."
translations.idiomatic: The eighth proposed that officials at court and throughout the provinces be ordered to submit honest counsel, so that the court might revive the enlightened example of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 其九以為「忠貞孝悌，宜擢以殊階；

translations.literal: The ninth held that "Loyalty, constancy, filial piety, and brotherly respect ought to be raised to special rank;
translations.idiomatic: The ninth held that men of loyalty, steadfastness, filial devotion, and fraternal duty should be promoted to exceptional rank;

sentences.zh: 清儉苦節，應授以政務」。

translations.literal: purity, frugality, and bitter integrity ought to be entrusted with government affairs."
translations.idiomatic: and that the pure, frugal, and stern in conduct should be given real responsibility in government."

sentences.zh: 其十以為「革命惟始，宜擇才北使」。

translations.literal: The tenth held that "The dynastic revolution has only begun; one ought to select talent to serve as envoys to the north."
translations.idiomatic: The tenth urged that, with the new dynasty barely established, gifted men should be chosen at once for missions to the northern courts.

sentences.zh: 其十一以為「交州險敻，要荒之表，宋末政苛，遂至怨叛。

translations.literal: The eleventh held that "Jiaozhou is perilous and remote, beyond the frontier of the wild borderlands; under the late Song government was harsh, until resentment led to rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The eleventh observed that Jiaozhou lay far off in rugged country beyond the edge of civilization, and that the Song court's harsh rule there had finally provoked revolt.

translations.literal: Now one ought to embrace them with kindness and grace; one should not yet trouble soldiers from afar and unsettle the border folk."
translations.idiomatic: The proper course now was to win the region with kindness, not to march troops from afar and unsettle the border people."

sentences.zh: 又撰賢聖雜語奏之，托以諷諫。

translations.literal: He also composed Miscellaneous Sayings of Sages and Worthies and submitted it, relying on it for indirect admonition.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled a collection of sage maxims and submitted it as veiled remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 上優詔答之。

translations.literal: The emperor replied with an excellent edict.
translations.idiomatic: The throne answered with a gracious imperial rescript.

sentences.zh: 又諫起宣陽門，表陳：「宜明守宰賞罰，立學校，制齊禮，開賓館以接鄰國。

translations.literal: He also remonstrated against raising the Xuanyang Gate and submitted a memorial stating: "One ought to make clear the rewards and punishments of prefects and magistrates, establish schools, standardize the rites of Qi, and open guest halls to receive neighboring states."
translations.idiomatic: He also opposed rebuilding the Xuanyang Gate and memorialized: "The court should clarify how local officials are rewarded and punished, found schools, unify ritual practice, and open guesthouses to receive envoys from neighboring states."

sentences.zh: 」上答曰：「夫賞罰以懲守宰，飾館以待遐荒，皆古之善政，吾所宜勉。

translations.literal: " The emperor replied: "Rewards and punishments to chasten prefects and magistrates, and guest halls adorned to await distant wilds—these are all excellent policies of antiquity, and what I ought to strive toward.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor answered: "Using reward and punishment to keep local officials in line, and fine guesthouses to welcome distant lands—these are ancient virtues I should indeed strive to match.

sentences.zh: 更撰新禮，或非易制。

translations.literal: To draft new rites anew may not be easy to accomplish at once.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting an entirely new ritual code, however, may not be easy to accomplish quickly.

sentences.zh: 國學之美，已敕公卿。

translations.literal: The excellence of the National University has already been ordered to the high ministers.
translations.idiomatic: As for restoring the National University, I have already charged the chief ministers with that task.

sentences.zh: 宣陽門今敕停。

translations.literal: The Xuanyang Gate is now ordered halted.
translations.idiomatic: Work on the Xuanyang Gate has been ordered stopped.

translations.idiomatic: My own virtue is thin and my failings many; I welcome further counsel."

sentences.zh: 善明身長七尺九寸，質素不好聲色，所居茅齋，斧木而已。

translations.literal: Shanming's body was seven feet nine inches in height; he was plain by nature and did not care for music and women; the dwelling he occupied was a thatched hut, with nothing but axe-hewn timber.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shanming stood seven feet nine inches tall. Plain by nature, he cared nothing for music or courtesans; he lived in a thatched cottage furnished with nothing but rough-hewn wood.

sentences.zh: 床榻几案，不加劃削。

translations.literal: Beds, couches, and tables received no planing or carving.
translations.idiomatic: His beds, couches, and tables were left unplaned and uncarved.

sentences.zh: 少立節行，常云：「在家當孝，為吏當清，子孫楷栻足矣。

translations.literal: From youth he established his conduct and often said: "At home one ought to be filial; in office one ought to be clean; for one's descendants to be a model is enough.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he held himself to a strict standard and often said, "Be filial at home and incorrupt in office; let your descendants take you as their measure, and that is enough.

sentences.zh: 」及累為州郡，頗黷財賄，崔祖思怪而問之，答曰：「管子雲，鮑叔知我。

translations.literal: " When he had repeatedly served in provinces and commanderies he was rather tainted with bribes; Cui Zusi wondered at it and questioned him, and he answered: "Master Guan said, 'Bao Shu knew me.'"
translations.idiomatic: " Yet after years in provincial office he had grown rather lax about gifts. Cui Zusi was astonished and asked why; he replied, "Guan Zhong said it: 'Bao Shu understood me.'"

sentences.zh: 」因流涕曰：「方寸亂矣，豈暇為廉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon, weeping, he said, "My heart is in turmoil; how could I have leisure to be incorrupt?
translations.idiomatic: " Then, weeping, he said, "My mind is in chaos; how could I spare a thought for honesty?

sentences.zh: 」所得金錢皆以贖母。

translations.literal: " All the money he obtained he used to ransom his mother.
translations.idiomatic: " Every coin he took went to ransom his mother from the north.

sentences.zh: 及母至，清節方峻。

translations.literal: When his mother arrived, his integrity became stern.
translations.idiomatic: Once she was home, his integrity became unbending.

sentences.zh: 所曆之職，廉簡不煩，俸祿散之親友。

translations.literal: In every post he held he was incorruptible and simple without fuss; his salary he distributed among kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: In every office he served he was spare and incorruptible, never troubling others, and he gave his salary away to kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 與崔祖思友善，祖思出為青冀二州，善明遺書敘舊，因相勖以忠概。

translations.literal: He was on friendly terms with Cui Zusi; when Zusi went out as governor of Qing and Ji, Shanming sent him a letter recalling their old friendship and thereby exhorted each other toward loyal magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: He and Cui Zusi were close friends. When Zusi left to govern Qing and Ji, Liu Shanming wrote recalling their old bond and urging each other to steadfast loyalty.

sentences.zh: 及聞祖思死，慟哭，仍得病。

translations.literal: When he heard that Zusi had died he wailed bitterly and forthwith fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: On learning of Zusi's death he mourned aloud and soon fell ill himself.

sentences.zh: 建元二年卒，遺命薄殯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan he died, leaving instructions for a plain burial.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Jianyuan, leaving orders for a simple funeral.

sentences.zh: 贈左將軍、豫州刺史，諡烈伯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Left General and Inspector of Yuzhou, with posthumous title Marquis Lie.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously appointed him Left General and Inspector of Yuzhou, with the posthumous title Marquis Lie.

sentences.zh: 子滌嗣。

translations.literal: His son Di succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Di inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 善明家無遺儲，唯有書八千卷。

translations.literal: Shanming's household had no surplus stores, only eight thousand scrolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shanming left no wealth behind, only eight thousand volumes in his library.

sentences.zh: 高帝聞其清貧，賜滌家葛塘屯穀五百斛，曰：「葛屯亦吾之垣下，令後世知其見異。」

translations.literal: The High Emperor, hearing of his purity and poverty, granted Di's household five hundred hu of grain from the Getang estate colony, saying: "Getang is also under my wall; let later ages know he was singled out for distinction."
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Di learned how poor he had been, he granted Di's family five hundred hu of grain from the Getang estate, saying, "Getang lies within my own domain; let posterity know how highly I regarded him."

sentences.zh: 善明從弟僧副字士雲，位前將軍，封豐陽男，卒于巴西、梓潼二郡太守。

translations.literal: Shanming's younger cousin Sengfu, style name Shiyun, held the post of Forward General and was enfeoffed as Baron of Fengyang; he died while serving as governor of the two commanderies Bazhong and Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shanming's cousin Liu Sengfu, styled Shiyun, rose to Forward General and was enfeoffed as Baron of Fengyang; he died in office as governor of Bazhong and Zitong.

sentences.zh: 上圖功臣像贊，僧副亦在焉。

translations.literal: When the emperor painted portraits of meritorious ministers with encomia, Sengfu was among them.
translations.idiomatic: When the court painted the portraits of meritorious ministers with laudatory inscriptions, Sengfu was included.

sentences.zh: 兄法護字士伯，有學業，位濟陰太守。

translations.literal: His elder brother Fahu, style name Shibo, had learning and held the post of Governor of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Fahu, styled Shibo, was a scholar and served as Governor of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 論曰：詩稱「抑抑威儀，惟人之則。

translations.literal: The commentary says: The Odes praise, "Stately, stately is the demeanor—such is man's rule."
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: The Book of Songs says, "Solemn and dignified is his bearing—such is the model for men."

sentences.zh: 」又云：「其儀不忒，正是四國。

translations.literal: " It also says: "His bearing without error—thus he rectifies the four states."
translations.idiomatic: " And again: "His conduct never falters—thus he sets the four quarters right."

sentences.zh: 」觀夫杲之風流所得，休野行己之度，蓋其有焉。

translations.literal: " Observing Gaozhi's elegant accomplishments gained and Xiuye's measure in personal conduct, broadly they possessed these.
translations.idiomatic: " In Yu Gaozhi's cultivated grace and Yu Bi's standard of conduct, one may see something of this.

sentences.zh: 仲和性履所遵，德璋業尚所守，殆人望也。

translations.literal: Zhonghe's nature and conduct followed, and Dezhang's pursuits and ideals upheld—they were nearly men of the people's expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen lived the life his character promised, and Kong Gui held to the ideals he professed; both were men the age looked up to.

sentences.zh: 懷珍宗族文質斌斌，自宋至梁，時移三代，或以隱節取高，或以文雅見重。

translations.literal: The Huaizhen clan, in literary and substantive quality splendidly blended, from Song through Liang across three generations' shift of time, some by reclusive integrity won elevation, some by elegant letters won weight.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu Huaizhen clan, blending culture and substance across three dynasties from Song to Liang, produced men who won honor through reclusive integrity and others who won renown through literary grace.

sentences.zh: 古人云立言立德，斯門其有之乎。

translations.literal: The ancients said that to establish words and to establish virtue—does this house perhaps have them?
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that a man should leave behind words and leave behind virtue—perhaps in this family one may find both.
